544783|2026-09.headline: E2E Networks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 43% QoQ to INR2,238 million, with EBITDA margin at 76.6% and PAT at INR727 million.
544783|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR2,238 million, up 411% YoY and 43% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR1,715 million (76.6% margin, up 141 bps QoQ). PAT rose to INR727 million from INR439 million in Q1, with PAT margin at 32.5%. Management attributed the gains to Blackwell GPU contribution, better utilisation and higher average realisation per GPU. Management declined to give guidance, utilisation, contracted-revenue mix or capex timing, and said the next B200 batch was expected to go live this quarter.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR439 million in Q1 (margin 28% in Q1)
vs loss of INR222 million in H1 FY26
vs loss of INR163 million in H1 FY26

segments.name: GPU cloud / Blackwell capacity
segments.commentary: Blackwell GPU contribution and higher average realisation per GPU drove the quarter. The existing B200 batch moved from pay-as-you-go to a multi-year contract of nearly INR1,000 crore running through June 2029, and the flagship Blackwell capacity is fully utilised under that contract.

segments.name: Sovereign AI platform (TIR and Jarvis)
segments.commentary: Management described the platform as the core of future growth and a full-stack offering for training, inference and agentic workloads. Blaze, Endpoint and Jarvis inference products are in soft release, with official launch a few weeks away.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given on MRR, exit rate, capex or utilisation; management said it does not give speculative capex guidance.
Management described the business as a 70%+ EBITDA margin business over the medium to long term, and said it sees no change in that target.
Next B200 batch (about 1,024 GPUs) expected to be deployed this quarter; no contract decided yet for that batch.
For uncontracted or short-term contracted capacity, management expects earnings to grow from the existing asset base.
Order-to-deployment cycle for GPUs is typically 3 to 6 months, per management.
capex_capacity: Next B200 batch of about 1,024 GPUs expected to go live in Q3 FY27 (current quarter); management said it expects deployment this quarter.
No visibility disclosed on B300 or Vera Rubin allotment for FY28-FY29; management will announce once plans are firm.
Management said it is open to debt as long as cash flow supports repayment, with no defined debt ceiling; future equity raise would be announced.
Management said it is open to off-balance-sheet GPU funding and to partnerships such as with L&T, with no specifics.
Some GPUs are used internally for R&D and platform build-out rather than sold.
demand_pricing: INR1,000 crore Blackwell contract with a sovereign AI customer runs through June 2029; it converts existing B200 capacity from pay-as-you-go to multi-year. Management would not say whether MRR is fully baked in, citing usage variability.
Management would not comment on the 85% gross margin reference, saying it is not a quarterly target; Q2 gross margin was about 88% per analyst framing.
Management declined to split revenue by inference, training or storage, and declined to quantify utilisation, citing volatility.
On GPU price increases, management gave no timeline for pass-through to MRR, stating it prioritises customer commitments and that earnings should grow on existing uncontracted assets.

Competition: management said the market is a global TAM of about USD 1 trillion and that there is no direct competition among a few players; it did not directly address domestic scale gaps versus players with large GPU fleets.

qa_highlights.question: When will the next B200 batch go live and when will revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the next B200 lot is expected to go live this quarter, hopefully soon, and it will inform investors when live.

qa_highlights.question: How much of current MRR of about INR75 crore comes from the INR1,000 crore contract, and is MRR fully baked in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contribution varies with usage but can be approximated from the INR1,000 crore value and contract period; it would not comment on incremental MRR.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the 88% gross margin, and where are operating costs going?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not sure about the 85% reference and reiterated a 70%+ EBITDA margin view for the medium to long term, without a quarterly target.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an MRR exit guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not give guidance and prefers to review past performance.

qa_highlights.question: What is India AI Mission revenue share and renewal pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: India AI customers were roughly 13% to 15% of Q2 revenue; management said it is building relationships beyond that programme.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international revenue mix and contracted revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: International was roughly 20% to 25% of Q2 revenue; management declined to share the contracted vs short-term split, calling it too volatile and with no target set.

qa_highlights.question: What debt levels is management comfortable with, and is there an equity raise under the INR1,500 crore enabling resolution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no defined upper limit on debt, provided front-end cash flow supports repayment and lender covenants are met; it would inform the market of any equity raise.

qa_highlights.question: What is utilisation and how does the TIR platform compare with global cloud offerings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is a point-in-time metric and that fleet-wide realisation is the better measure; it said platform competitiveness should be judged over the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Indian competitive landscape, with rivals at about 90,000 and 8,000 GPUs, affect E2E?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it operates in a global market of about USD 1 trillion TAM and that there is enough demand for everyone, without addressing relative scale directly.

qa_highlights.question: Will the economics change when customers move to platform-based (not raw compute) offerings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this would be answered over time and gave no margin, realisation or ROC numbers; it said most GPUs today run on its platforms with very little bare metal sold.

Unclear funding plans for future GPU capex (debt, off-balance-sheet, equity), and no B300 or Vera Rubin visibility for FY28-FY29.
Management time-limited responses on the 85% gross margin reference, leaving sustainability unclear.

544785|2026-03.headline: Hexagon Nutrition FY26 revenue rose 17.8% to INR382.63 crores, EBITDA margin expanded to 13.83% and PAT grew 56.1% to INR37.94 crores.
544785|2026-03.overview: This was the maiden earnings call after the company's NSE and BSE listing, covering Q4 and FY26 results. Management reported FY26 revenue of INR382.63 crores (up 17.8%), EBITDA of INR52.90 crores (up 32.01%) and PAT of INR37.94 crores (up 56.1%). Q4 revenue was INR115.04 crores, Q4 EBITDA INR15.35 crores (13.34% margin) and Q4 PAT INR10.9 crores (9.5% margin). Management attributed margin gains to branded product mix, premix growth and manufacturing efficiencies, and guided to continued margin expansion, though much of the call was qualitative and some figures were stated loosely.

financial_highlights.change: vs about INR60 crores last year

segments.name: Branded / clinical and consumer nutrition (PentaSure, PediaGold, Obesigo)
segments.commentary: About 30% of FY26 revenue per CFO, with gross margins cited at 60-68%; operates at 50-60% utilisation. Management says it expanded from roughly 10% of revenue to 30%.

segments.name: Micronutrient premixes (B2B to pharma and FMCG)
segments.commentary: About 35-40% of FY26 revenue; EBITDA margin guided at 35-40%; utilisation around 40-45%. Premix domestic order jump was dispatched largely in Q4.

segments.name: ESG segment (RUTF, RUSF, micronutrient powders)
segments.commentary: About 30% of FY26 revenue; margin guided at 25-30%; utilisation 35-40%, sometimes up to 60%, depending on order flow. Large orders dispatched in Q4 added to receivables.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to maintain the growth momentum of the last two to three years and some margin expansion as operating leverage improves.
Blended capacity utilisation expected at 35-40% for year-end and going forward, up from 30% (figure cited as YTD December).
Management said revenue growth aspiration over 3-5 years is roughly a doubling of the business, consistent with the past four to five years (CEO-level confirmation: 'correct estimate').
Management said West Asia war has not significantly hurt business and it expects to continue its growth journey in FY27; Q1 may be affected, per analyst framing.
Tender-based (UN) business has a healthy order pipeline, so utilisation is expected to improve over time.
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation about 30% per presentation (YTD December), expected to reach 35-40% for year-end; branded 50-60%, premix 40-45%, ESG 35-40%.
Management said it keeps a capacity buffer for future tenders and unanticipated orders.
Manufacturing sites in Nashik (Maharashtra) and Chennai (Tamil Nadu MEPZ-SEZ). Wholly owned subsidiaries in South Africa, India, Uzbekistan and Hong Kong.
Analyst referenced chronic underutilisation of 37% cited in the DRHP, attributed to UN tenders; no capex amount or commissioning timeline was given.
Management said it will strengthen manufacturing capabilities where required but gave no capex quantum.
demand_pricing: Exports are about 57% of revenue; more than 80% of exports come from premixes and ESG, with the balance from branded exports. West Asia is under 20% of exports.
Imports are under 25% of raw material requirements, mainly vitamins (A, B-group, C, folic acid) from China, Singapore, Korea and Europe. No significant sourcing challenges reported.

Clinical nutrition market size cited at about INR6,300 crores; management says the company is a small share. Growth plans include more medical representatives, Tier 2/3 expansion, e-commerce (Amazon, Flipkart, e-pharmacies) and medical marketing.
Whey price increase handled by passing it through to MRPs in branded; vitamins are hedged via strategic inventory. No major impact so far.
Competitors in premixes: DSM, Firmenich, BASF, SternVitamin, Piramal. In branded, MNCs Abbott, Nestle and Fresenius Kabi. Management declined to give a market share figure.

qa_highlights.question: Split of export revenue by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 80% of exports come from premixes and ESG; the balance is branded exports. Brand names were not disclosed as customer permissions were not obtained.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and what drove EBITDA margin from 6.2% to 13.8% over four years?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said branded products (gross margin above 50%) were the main driver, with premixes adding support and growing about 20-30% over four years.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to maintain recent momentum and expand margins by segment: branded 60-68%, premix 35-40%, ESG 25-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation outlook and UN tender dynamics?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended utilisation of about 30% is YTD December; expected at 35-40% for year-end. Tender business has a healthy pipeline, so utilisation should improve.

qa_highlights.question: Rise in trade receivables from INR60 crores to about INR82 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by large ESG orders dispatched in the last quarter and a domestic premix order jump dispatched mostly in Q4; management says these have normalised.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 export growth outlook given West Asia war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the war has not negatively affected the business and it expects to continue the growth journey, with no quantified FY27 guidance.

risks_watch: Receivables jumped to about INR82 crores from INR60 crores; watch for normalisation and collection days in FY27.
Raw material exposure: imported vitamins (under 25% of inputs) and whey price volatility; pass-through only in branded.
Geopolitical risk: West Asia accounts for under 20% of exports; Q1 FY27 impact possible.
Low blended utilisation (about 30%) and reliance on lumpy UN/tender orders make volume and absorption uncertain.
Competition from DSM, BASF, Firmenich, Piramal in premixes and Abbott, Nestle, Fresenius Kabi in branded; brand penetration of PediaGold and Obesigo is low.
Management did not quantify FY27 revenue or margin guidance and gave no capex plan.

544785|2026-06.headline: Hexagon Nutrition Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 43.2% YoY to INR104.3 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.3% from 13.8%.
544785|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 43.2% YoY to INR104.3 crore, with volume growth of roughly 25-40% across premix and branded segments. EBITDA rose 17.3% to INR11.8 crore, but margin compressed about 250 bps to 11.3% on higher raw material costs (West Asia crisis) and elevated selling, distribution and freight spend. PAT grew 25.1% to INR8.1 crore. Management guided FY27 growth of 20-25%, flagged a INR100 crore order book for Q2-Q3, and said MRP increases of 10-15% on some branded products will help margins from Q2.

financial_highlights.value: Contracted by more than 3 percentage points YoY
financial_highlights.change: Attributed to raw material cost rise

segments.name: Premix (micronutrient)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 62% of Q1 revenue; grew about 55% YoY per CFO. Over 50% of plant capacity utilisation is attributed to premix, and the INR100 crore order book is about 70-75% premix and ESG combined.

segments.name: Branded (clinical/wellness, B2C)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 28% of revenue; grew about 22% YoY (CFO) or about 28% (Dr. Nikhil). Branded share rose from 18% to 20%, 25% and about 30% over recent years. Target of 35% of revenue in the next couple of years; B2C revenue has crossed INR100 crore per an analyst question.

segments.name: Therapeutic nutrition / ESG (RUTF, RUSF, MNP)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 10% of revenue; grew about 42% YoY. Tender-based, so order flows vary quarter to quarter. ESG pipeline cited at INR75-100 crore for the remaining year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 20-25%, same trajectory as last year; management called this the conservative side.
Q2 supported by an order book of about INR100 crore, to be executed in Q2 and partly in Q3.
Seasonality: Q1 and Q2 build momentum, with the main growth in Q3 and Q4 per management.
MRP increases of 10-15% on some branded products will affect margins from Q2; gross margin expected to ease over the next two quarters.
Field force investment (over 50% increase YoY) expected to show productivity in roughly two to three quarters, with operating leverage by end of Q3.
Nashik premix facility redevelopment capex of INR25-30 crore over one to one-and-a-half years; about 70% to be funded by long-term bank borrowing.
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation about 47% (rising from around 30% previously stated); management cautioned segment rates vary, with some lines at 35-40% and others around 65%.
Nashik about 55-60% utilised, Tuticorin about 35-40%, Chennai about 25-30%; Uzbekistan has limited order book for Q2-Q3 and is not material yet.
Nashik premix facility being demolished and rebuilt; capex INR25-30 crore over the next 1-1.5 years.
Management says manufacturing capacity suffices for the next two to three years of growth.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of roughly 25-40% YoY in Q1 across premix and branded; management said price hikes were not the main driver.
Raw material cost pressure: about 25-30% of raw materials are imported; whey protein costs rose sharply, while some vitamins were stable.
Freight costs rose due to the West Asia situation; West Asia is under 20% of exports.
Export concentration: top 3-5 countries make up about 25-40% of exports; growth in Central Asia and Africa, with Europe and North America targeted.
Branded MRP raised 10-15% on some products to pass on raw material costs.
Inventory build partly strategic due to rising product prices and ESG/premix order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a slowdown expected given 43% Q1 growth versus 20-25% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Nikhil said Q2 is supported by a INR100 crore order book, with no sign of slowdown; Q1 and Q2 build momentum and Q3-Q4 carry the main growth. CFO called 20-25% the conservative side.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin contract, and will it normalise from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed a more than 3 percentage point gross margin contraction to West Asia-driven raw material cost increases in premix and branded. Management is passing costs to customers via MRP increases and hopes margins normalise from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly freight costs from the geopolitical situation, plus field force and marketing investment; over 50% more field force versus last year, treated as an investment that will pay off in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and its timing?
qa_highlights.answer: INR100 crore order book, to execute in Q2 and partly Q3; about 70-75% premix and ESG, rest branded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and what is the bottleneck?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended utilisation about 47% (40-47% range cited); premix in 25 kg bags versus branded sachets and tins take different times, so segment-level rates vary widely.

qa_highlights.question: What are the biggest constraints to growth over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Nikhil said manufacturing capacity and working capital are not constraints; distribution expansion into Tier 2-3 cities is the focus, with operating leverage expected in a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression (11.3% vs 13.8%) persists if raw material and freight costs stay high or MRP hikes lag.
Inventory days rose to about 142 from about 130+; strategic stocking may tie up working capital.
Tender-based ESG orders create quarter-to-quarter volatility.
Field force and distribution costs ahead of productivity; leverage expected only by end of Q3.
Branded share target of 35% of revenue in a couple of years; growth needs to keep pace with 20-25% guidance.
West Asia geopolitical risk on freight, raw material costs and exports.

544793|2026-06.headline: Susan Electricals Q1 FY27 revenue rose 279% YoY to ₹95.36 Cr and PAT turned positive at ₹6.39 Cr, with blended operating margin ~11.9%.
544793|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 279% YoY to ₹95.36 Cr and operating profit rose 980% YoY to ₹11.04 Cr, with PAT of ₹6.39 Cr versus a ₹0.42 Cr loss a year earlier. Management attributed the improvement to higher scale, better product mix and higher EBITDA per unit. Management is shifting the mix toward HT/MVCC and LT cables and is adding 4,500 Km p.a. of capacity (+60%) with commercial operations targeted from Feb 2027. Management declined to give a FY27 revenue number, and several answers on margins and product mix were inconsistent between the prepared remarks and the Q&A.

segments.name: LT cables and conductors
segments.commentary: Management cited ~6.5% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27. Company said winding wires and LT/conductors typically earn 10-15% per unit.

segments.name: HT cables
segments.commentary: Management cited ~7% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27. HT/MVCC currently make up ~5-10% of revenue (another answer said 10-15%).

segments.name: Winding wires

544799|2026-06.headline: Turtlemint's first post-listing call: FY26 revenue up 57% to INR 1,098 crores, Q4 first adjusted-EBITDA breakeven quarter (INR 60 crores service EBITDA).
544799|2026-06.overview: Management reported FY26 platform premium of INR 3,868 crores (up 31% YoY) and operating revenue of INR 1,098 crores (up 57%). Service EBITDA rose 70% to INR 142 crores (about 13% of revenue), and Q4 revenue of INR 357 crores (up 42%) delivered the company's first breakeven quarter at adjusted EBITDA on a consolidated basis. Corporate overheads fell to 23% of revenue in FY26 from 38% in FY25, and PAT before exceptional items was INR 129 crores. Management declined formal guidance but said FY27 should be profitable on a full-year consolidated basis and that losses or profitability gaps would improve by more than 40%.

segments.name: Insurance distribution (PoSP / Turtlemint Insurance Broking)
segments.commentary: About 97% of FY26 revenue is commission from the broking subsidiary; PoSP premium grew more than 40% in FY26. General insurance is more than 90% of platform premium (revenue split is 90% GI, 10% non-GI per management); health grew more than 60%.

segments.name: Turtlefin (enterprise)
segments.commentary: Enterprise partners (banks, NBFCs, fintechs) contribute about 20% of platform premium, roughly INR 770 crores by the analyst's arithmetic. Take rate is low, transaction-based, and management called it high margin with no direct variable cost.

segments.name: Adjacencies (mutual funds, loans)
segments.commentary: Mutual fund AUM about INR 1,400 crores through the subsidiary; loan disbursement run rate about INR 300 crores annualised, recently launched. Non-insurance businesses are about 3% of FY26 revenue.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; board decided not to give future guidance, but management gave directional color.
FY27: management expects to reduce losses or improve profitability by more than 40% and to be profitable on a full-year consolidated basis; each quarter expected to exceed the prior one.
FY27 corporate overheads expected to grow with inflation rather than volumes; no exceptional items expected in FY27.

Medium term (about five years / FY30): service EBITDA expected to rise from 13-14% to about 24-25% of revenue, corporate overheads to fall to sub 5-6% of revenue, giving EBITDA/PBT/PAT of about 18-20% of revenue.
Long-run growth framed as continuing the historical 40%-plus CAGR in revenue and key KPIs; dividend policy possible after one to two years of sustained profitability.
capex_capacity: Balance sheet has few fixed assets (IT equipment, offices); no costs are capitalised, all expensed.
Digital partner base: 93,000+ P3M active at 31 March 2026 (51% CAGR over seven years); about 6.5 lakh verified DPs; 46 insurers (45+ partners per Q&A); coverage across 19,000+ PIN codes.
Turtlemint Academy averages 52,000+ monthly active users and 6,500+ training hours per month; certifies over 5,000 new sellers per month.
Insurance Hub gives paperless policy issuance across 40+ insurers; 8 lakh+ quotes generated daily.
Agentic AI and LLM automation under development for support tickets, renewal calling, claims and activation; more updates promised.
demand_pricing: Growth drivers: recruitment of new DPs (about 80% non-insurance background, mostly under 35) plus productivity gains in existing cohorts (frontline premium productivity up 20%+ YoY).

Health insurance growth above 60-75% helped by affordability tailwinds and GST cuts; commissions were cut in Oct-Dec quarter and management says the platform passed these through without slowing volume.
Renewal rates in Q4 were significantly higher than in the same quarter of the prior year; management says renewal rates are above industry averages.
Insurer concentration is low: top 3 insurers about 22% of business; top 100 DPs generated 4.62% of platform premium.
Claims desk settled over INR 85 crores of delayed or rejected claims in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove FY26 premium and revenue growth, and is it sustainable given the high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited DP recruitment and productivity, the renewal book, and health tailwinds; H1 growth was flattered by base effects, Q4 growth (about 42%) is closer to steady state, and management expects historical 40%-plus growth to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How would commission regulation changes affect the business, and how are PoSPs classified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the asset-light model incurs costs only after a transaction, so commission changes are passed down, as shown in the Oct-Dec GST period. It could not say how the regulator will classify PoSPs as agents or brokers.

qa_highlights.question: How does Turtlemint recruit DPs amid competition, and what is the TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of DPs come from non-insurance backgrounds with 60-65 profiles; onboarding is digital plus a pan-India branch network. Management did not quantify TAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of the enterprise (Turtlefin) business and its take rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Enterprise premium is about 20% of platform premium (about INR 770 crores by the analyst's arithmetic). The take rate is low but volume-based and high margin, since tech is already built and licensed; enterprise growth should accelerate as new accounts go live.

qa_highlights.question: Renewal vs new service EBITDA margin, and renewal share?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal service EBITDA margin is about 2.5-3x the new business margin. Renewal revenue is INR 225 crores; management declined to disclose renewal premium.

qa_highlights.question: Non-insurance revenue share and the other financial products?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-insurance is about 3% of FY26 revenue. Mutual fund AUM is about INR 1,400 crores and loan disbursement run rate about INR 300 crores annualised; the incremental revenue drops straight to service EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to the 18-20% long-term EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Service EBITDA is 13-14% today and is expected to reach 24-25% in a few years, with corporate overheads held at sub 5-6% of revenue for FY30.

544802|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 net profit Rs.22.77 Crores (~12% margin) on 105% load factor, with fuel costs the main EBITDA drag.
544802|2026-06.overview: Management attributed the quarter to a Middle East-driven spike in fuel prices, which took roughly Rs.14 crores out of EBITDA, while load factor rose to 105% and average ticket price rose about 4.3% year on year. Guests served exceeded 55,700 and staterooms booked reached 24,245, up about 10%. Management expects fuel surcharges on new bookings to show up from end-Q2/early-Q3, and says the second ship (Cordelia Sky) brings a much higher suite count. Finance cost roughly doubled to about Rs.4 crores on a bank loan taken to support rating and FD-backed arrangements.

segments.name: Empress (existing ship)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth for June 2026 vs June 2025 estimated at about 8-9% by management; expected to move to 10-12% going forward. Empress has about 69 suite and balcony cabins and about 800 total cabins.

segments.name: Cordelia Sky (new ship)
segments.commentary: Expected to have about 269 suite and balcony cabins and about 1,000 total cabins, with nine restaurants versus three on Empress. Management says revenue potential per ship is almost 100% higher than the current vessel.

Fuel surcharges on new bookings expected to recover most of the extra fuel cost, with impact visible from end-Q2 / beginning of Q3.
Management is hopeful that the extra fuel cost will be offset by year-end through additional savings, as fuel prices move toward forecast levels.
Management says it is planning on an annual-average basis rather than quarterly, and Q2 is being used as a lower-capacity test period for new itineraries without affecting annual results.
Cost sharing across three ships (fixed shore-side marketing and management fees) expected to lower per-ship cost once the fleet is fully operational.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main driver is fuel, worth about Rs.14 crores; crew wage increases of about Rs.2 crores (about 16% in percentage terms) and food costs of about Rs.1 crore were smaller items.

qa_highlights.question: How will higher fuel costs be passed on to customers given advance bookings?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel surcharges apply to new bookings only, not already-sold Q1 cruises, so recovery shows from end-Q2/beginning-Q3. Fuel was pre-ordered and bought at prices that management says have fallen from the peak.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 revenue growth from occupancy or ticket price?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: load factor rose from 99.9% to 105% and average ticket price rose about 4%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost roughly double?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a loan was taken from IDFC First Bank, backed by FDs, to support rating requirements; it carries a 1% prepayment cost and is being carried over, with the company citing zero net debt given matching FD assets.

qa_highlights.question: Expected Q2 top-line run rate versus about Rs.190 crores in Q1, and like-for-like Empress growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a numeric Q2 run rate, pointing to cabin mix. Empress growth was about 8-9% in the quarter, expected to reach 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy to expand margins beyond fuel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed shore-side marketing, management fees and other costs will be spread across three ships as the fleet grows, with better purchasing power.

544814|2026-06.headline: Knack Packaging Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 40.5% YoY to INR2,647.7 million, with EBITDA up 53.1% and margin at 22.35%.
544814|2026-06.overview: Knack Packaging reported Q1 FY27 as its first earnings call after listing on NSE and BSE. Consolidated revenue grew 40.5% YoY on 20.9% higher volume (10,940 MT), with EBITDA up 53.1% and PAT up 47.96%. Management attributed margin gains to operating leverage, cost discipline, solar power and a rising share of pinch-bottom bags. Capacity utilisation is about 91%, with a rented plant added to bridge until the IPO-funded plant, targeted for October 2027, takes installed capacity to about 70,000 MT.

Management expects Q1 FY27 sales levels to be maintained until the new plant starts, using the rented facilities.

Main construction of the new plant is expected to pick up after the monsoon; machinery finalisation is ongoing.

11 MW solar farm at Khedbrahma started in the last quarter; electricity cost fell about 1.1% of revenue YoY from solar.
Gross block rose to INR416 crore, with INR141 crore added over the year; the IPO proceeds are about INR320 crore.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR130 crore cited by management.
Customer retention is about 90%; more than 2,000 customers and over 13,000 SKUs.
Cargill is about 12-17% of revenue (figures varied on the call), with about 600 SKUs and a contract of 2 years plus a 1-year extension, priced as polymer cost plus conversion.
About 45-50% of customers are on fixed conversion-cost pricing with raw material pass-through; the rest are small buyers with pass-through pricing on the day of change.
Management said it passes polymer price changes through to customers on the same day, and that about 50% of input cost changes are passed on, with about 60% retained in some cases.

Management claims about 10% market share in the Indian bag segment (per a Technopack report), and says it is the leader in pinch-bottom bags in India. Management named Polytex (USA) as its only direct listed peer.

qa_highlights.answer: Cargill (USA) business grew from INR4 crore in 2020 to about INR140 crore; it is on a 2+1-year contract and buys finished bags. Management cited the cost of packaging below 1% of product value. FX gain in Q1 FY27 was INR1.6 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited EBITDA per kg of about INR54 in Q1 and INR45 in FY26. Pinch-bottom share is 22.5-23% and is rising; the call did not give a 70,000 MT utilisation timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth be sustained in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q1 sales levels to hold as the rented plants run until the new plant starts in October 2027. It said the onboarding process for new products is long, so marketing is being increased through rented capacity.

544814|2026-09.headline: Knack Packaging Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 52.5% to INR294.76 crores, but EBITDA margin fell 285 bps to 16.35% on polymer cost pass-through lag.

PAT rose 21.2% to INR25.02 crores, though it absorbed a INR2.62 crores share of loss from the Sayem Knack JV in Mexico. Management expects margin recovery from Q3 FY27 as price revisions flow through, subject to market stabilisation.

544822|2026-06.headline: Laser Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR5,215 million and EBITDA 26% to INR659 million, with EPC revenue up 129%.
544822|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 15% YoY to INR5,215 million, with EBITDA up 26% to INR659 million and margin expanding to 12.6% from 11.5%. Growth came mainly from EPC (revenue up 129% to INR1,391 million), while manufacturing revenue fell slightly to INR3,824 million from INR3,932 million. Finance cost of INR362 million absorbed about 55% of EBITDA, and PAT was INR211 million. Management said the IPO-funded debt repayment of about INR4,900 million, completed in Q2 FY27, will lower finance cost from later quarters; the company did not give numerical guidance for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR296 million YoY; about 55% of EBITDA
manufacturing INR14,327 million; EPC INR13,557 million

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3,824 million (vs INR3,932 million YoY), EBITDA about INR388 million, implying roughly 10% margin. Management described manufacturing profitability as broadly stable; cable-to-conductor split is about 90:10.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,391 million (+129% YoY) and EBITDA INR276 million (vs INR93 million), a margin of about 20%. Management said quarterly EPC margins can vary and guided to a typical range of 15-20%.

guidance_outlook: No specific FY27 guidance given; management pointed to a long-run revenue growth of about 15-16% (5-year CAGR) and said EBITDA margins should stay stable.
Debt repayment of about INR4,900 million from IPO proceeds was completed in Q2 FY27; gross debt is about INR3,600 million and fixed deposits about INR2,400 million, leaving net debt negligible.
Annualised interest saving of roughly INR40 crore at PBT level, based on about 9% cost of debt on INR490 crore repaid.
Deferred tax benefit from FY23 carry-forward losses (about INR125-130 crore in total) to be used up in FY27; cash taxes resume from FY28.
Working capital days typically 100-120; management expects the INR8,000 million of projects started in Q4 FY26 to work through over coming quarters.
capex_capacity: Three manufacturing units with aggregate installed capacity of about 85,000 metric tons (up from about 62,000 metric tons three years earlier, per an analyst question).
Current capacity utilisation at about 62% per management's answer to an analyst's question on overall utilisation; cable utilisation was described as roughly 80% in an analyst question.
Management's strategy is to add capacity once utilisation reaches about 75-80%; the 85,000 MT figure is an optimised rating, with 90-95% achievable.
Capex will be phased and tied to customer demand; the company holds land within its factory footprint for future expansion.
Built extra capacity for AECC/HTLS products ahead of orders; utilisation may stay low initially before settling.
demand_pricing: India's conductor market reportedly grew from about 102 billion (FY20) to about 185 billion (FY25), with 230-250 billion expected by FY30 (CRISIL, as cited by management).

Utilities floated tenders worth about INR3,500 crore for HTLS conductors and re-conductoring in the last year; Laser has bid for about INR1,250 crore. Bids are under evaluation and no HTLS revenue has been booked yet.
High-voltage cables rose from 9% to about 29% of total revenue over the last nine quarters, per management.
Management estimated EBITDA margin difference of about 2-3 points between normal and HT cables; conventional conductors are the lowest-margin product.
EPC revenue is 100% from government and utility customers; manufacturing is about 50:50 government and private.

qa_highlights.question: Expected margin expansion over 12-18 months from new conductor products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to remain stable, with revenue growing at around 15-16% as in the past five years; HTLS revenue should improve margins once prices open, but no timeline was given beyond 'next few quarters'.

qa_highlights.question: Interest saving after IPO debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR40 crore a year at PBT level, based on a roughly 9% cost of capital and INR490 crore repaid.

qa_highlights.question: Are Laser the only bidders for the TS-technology re-conductoring tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Not necessarily; tenders are technology-neutral, and some have few bidders and others many. Management said Laser's technology tie-up from March 2025 gave it the headroom to bid.

qa_highlights.question: Why has production stayed flat while capacity rose from 62,000 to 85,400 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: The mix has shifted to specialised, higher-value products that are lower in volume but add to revenue and profit.

qa_highlights.question: Tax: what is the deferred tax position?
qa_highlights.answer: Carry-forward losses from an FY23 acquisition give a tax saving of about INR125-130 crore, booked as deferred tax; cash taxes start after FY27, and P&L tax expense is already stated after tax.

risks_watch: Finance cost (INR362 million, 55% of EBITDA in Q1) must fall after the debt repayment for PAT to convert better; the Q1 figure does not yet include the benefit.
Working capital build: about INR90 crore of FG and WIP inventory rise in June 2026, and a near-zero operating cash flow in Q1.
Outcome of about INR1,250 crore of HTLS/re-conductoring tenders, which are the main driver of the new product thesis.
Manufacturing revenue declined YoY, and production volumes were roughly flat over three years despite higher capacity.
Reliance on government/utility customers; EPC revenue is entirely government-sourced.
Reporting is standalone; one SPV subsidiary has nil revenue. An analyst pointed out that a prior-year one-time gain of about INR32 crore distorts the PAT comparison.

rows.why: HTLS/AECC products are already built ahead of orders, with about INR1,250 crore of bids under evaluation against a INR3,500 crore tender pool, but no HTLS revenue has been booked and no timeline was given.

rows.why: Laser has bid for about INR1,250 crore of the roughly INR3,500 crore utility tenders, which are still under evaluation, and these are the main driver of the new-product thesis, though no HTLS revenue has been booked yet.

544824|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 6% YoY to a 60% sequential rise; closing order book reached ₹626 crores, up 57% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 36.1%.
544824|2026-09.overview: Management framed Q2 FY27 as resilient: revenue grew 6% YoY and rose sharply QoQ, while H1 FY27 revenue grew 18% YoY, driven by aftermarket and defence. Product revenue was lower YoY on customer delivery timing and supply chain factors. EBITDA margin was 36.1% in Q2 and 35.7% in H1, down YoY on mix and people costs but up sequentially. Order inflows were strong (H1 ₹330 crores, up 95% YoY), and capex is largely complete, with growth to be funded mainly from internal accruals.

financial_highlights.value: Q2 up ~41% YoY; H1 up 29% YoY; 27% of revenue in H1

financial_highlights.metric: Free cash flow after capex (H1 FY27)

financial_highlights.value: ₹36 crores in Q2 FY27 vs ₹12 crores in Q1 FY27

segments.name: Industrial Gears (product)
segments.commentary: Product revenue was lower YoY on delivery timing and supply chain factors; management says gearbox orders deliver in a 6-8 month cycle. Of the ₹626 crores order book, ₹156 crores is for FY27 from Gears.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue up ~41% YoY and H1 up 29%, contributing 27% of H1 revenue. Management is building export aftermarket via hiring and agent partnerships; aftermarket orders deliver in 3-6 months.

segments.name: Defence and Marine
segments.commentary: Defence revenue scaled meaningfully from a low base (analyst cited 3.3x YoY in Q2 and 4.7x in H1; company did not give absolute figures). Of the ₹626 crores order book, ₹81 crores is for FY27 from Defence; defence orders are lumpy with 12-month or longer cycles.

guidance_outlook: No revenue or margin guidance given; management declined to give FY27 or FY28 forecasts.
Medium-term ambition: growth above 25% YoY (CAGR) over the next five to seven years.
Management expects EBITDA margin to stay at 35% or above over the medium to long term and does not expect defence/aftermarket mix shift to be margin dilutive.
Some H2 book-and-bill is needed to meet internal targets; management says it is secured. Orders pushed from Q2 to Q3 FY27; Q3 and Q4 outlook described as 'extremely encouraging'.
Further capex expected to be balancing, routine and small capacity enhancements, not substantial; next capex trigger at about 80-85% capacity utilisation.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex ₹41 crores; the ₹340 crores capex programme (split evenly between gears and defence) is almost fully complete.
Combined capex is said to support production of about ₹700 crores based on gearbox mix, plus defence capability revenue (defence figure not disclosed).
Next capacity trigger is 80-85% utilisation; management declined to say when that would be reached.
New defence facility inaugurated; management expects production there to support defence growth over coming quarters.
Data-centre and space gearbox product expected to be ready for launch in the current quarter.
demand_pricing: Middle East and African orders were significant in Q2; delayed STG pump and Middle East orders expected to finalise, timing shifting quarter to quarter. Management cited ADNOC pump and compressor orders via OEMs.
Global high-speed industrial gearbox market (OEM plus aftermarket) about $1.1 billion in 2026, growing 6-7% through 2033; 7-9 global competitors ex-China, largest with about 15% share.

Competition: a global competitor in South India has been present for a few years; management says TPTL's market share is unchanged. Indian compressor gear market is small; compressor competition is mainly in Europe.
Domestic compressor and gearbox demand tied to oil and gas capex; management said oil at $120 is an opportunity, and TPTL is qualified with ADNOC.
Defence procurement: FY27 Ministry of Defence allocation ₹7.85 lakh crore; defence capital outlay ₹2.19 lakh crore (21.8% above FY26 BE); ₹1.39 lakh crore earmarked for domestic industry procurement.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ₹626 crore order book is scheduled for H2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not split by quarter. It said ₹156 crores of the book is for FY27 from Gears and ₹81 crores from Defence.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin decline from ~45% to ~36% finished, given people costs?

qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose defence segment revenue; it said segment reporting may be considered in the future.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term growth outlook and book-and-bill for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no FY27 numbers; medium-term ambition is above 25% CAGR over five to seven years. Some H2 book-and-bill is needed and management says it is secured.

qa_highlights.question: Export order book and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Export product orders rose to ₹36 crores in Q2 from ₹12 crores in Q1. Management expects significant expansion over coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will utilisation reach full capacity by FY29-FY30, and when is the next capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a timeline; next capex phase triggered at about 80-85% utilisation, which has not yet been reached.

Working capital remains high at 188 core days; receivables and inventory build may move with project milestones.

Next quarter: order conversion into revenue, export order momentum, defence order wins, and data-centre product launch.

544829|2026-06.headline: SBI Funds Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 15% YoY to ₹1,149 crore and PAT reached ₹873 crore, up 37% QoQ.
544829|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first earnings call after the company's IPO listing. Mutual fund QAAUM reached ₹12.6 trillion (up 11% YoY) with a 15.1% overall market share, while operating revenue of ₹1,149 crore and operating profit of ₹907 crore grew 15% and 17% YoY. Management attributed margin gains mainly to asset-mix shift from passive funds toward equity, hybrid, arbitrage and gold/silver ETFs, and said the TER cut was passed on to distributors with a net neutral-to-positive effect. Management declined to give guidance, citing the silent period.

segments.name: Mutual fund (core)
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 90-92% of operating revenue. Equity yield stated at 62 bps; gold and silver ETFs earn about 44-45 bps spread; arbitrage fund yield about 30 bps versus about 11 bps for liquid funds.

segments.name: Alternates (PMS, advisory, international, AIF)
segments.commentary: Together about 8% of operating revenue. Management said AIF and PMS are more attractive than equity on margin, and the company plans one more AIF product this quarter.

segments.name: Passive
segments.commentary: Passive QAAUM ₹4 trillion, up 12% YoY; management said low-yield passive concentration has declined, adding about 2 bps to overall margin.

guidance_outlook: No quantitative guidance given; management cited the silent period for QAAUM, opex and ESOP details.
Second SIF strategy (Ex-Top 100 long-short) to launch this quarter; SBI Balanced Hybrid Fund being launched; SBI Nifty Midcap 150 Momentum 50 ETF FOF NFO underway.
Management expects SBI channel share of SIP flows to remain about one-third, with the aim of holding a 35:65 split versus other and direct channels.
Opex to focus on technology, AI and human resources; training costs expected to rise in Q2-Q3 FY27.
Management reiterated a new public dividend policy has been published; payout subject to board and AGM approval.
capex_capacity: Management said 94% of investor transactions are processed digitally on a hybrid cloud infrastructure.
About 50,000 distributors now use the partner app and portal for analytics and reporting.
In-house research platform Neo is being enhanced with AI capabilities.
Distribution footprint: over 23,000 SBI branches, over 124,000 independent financial advisors, nearly 10,000 national distributors, over 90 banking partners; coverage of 98%+ pin codes.
Alternate business hiring underway; one more AIF product to be launched this quarter.
demand_pricing: Industry QAAUM grew about 15% YoY and was broadly stable QoQ; industry monthly SIP inflows above ₹31,000 crore.
Fresh SIPs added in the quarter were 1.7 million (about 16 lakh); live SIPs reached 16 million.

B30 locations: management cited 19% MAAUM market share and more than 25% B30 market share; about 65% of SIP count and 44% of SIP amount from B30; about ₹2,500 crore of the ₹4,000 crore monthly SIP flow.
Flow market share is in line with AUM market share; equity and hybrid market share around 11-12%.
TER reduction under the new regulation was passed to distributors from April, with management calling the net effect neutral to slightly positive.

qa_highlights.answer: Mutual funds contribute about 90-92% of operating revenue; PMS, advisory and international make up about 8%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said TER pass-through was neutral and not the driver. Margin gains came from asset mix: lower passive share replaced by equity and hybrid, adding about 2 bps to overall yield.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP flows slip slightly from March to June?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the flattish trend to market volatility and geopolitical conditions; monthly SIP flow of about ₹4,000 crore was maintained.

qa_highlights.answer: SBI contributes about 35% of active equity AUM and about 20% of overall AUM. SBI channel share of SIP flow is about one-third (₹1,300 crore of ₹4,000 crore); management aims to keep this split.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost decline of 1% YoY sustainable; when do salary increments come in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline reflects the new labour code implementation; training costs will rise in Q2 and Q3, and employee benefits are unchanged.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said alternates are more selective and more attractive than equity on margin, with easier regulation.

544847|2026-06.headline: Manipal Health Q1 FY27 revenue rose over 38% YoY to INR3,091 crores, with network EBITDA of INR749 crores (up over 26%), volume-led.
544847|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's first earnings call after listing. Revenue was INR3,091 crores (up over 38% YoY) and network EBITDA INR749 crores (up over 26%; over 30% excluding a one-off gain in Q1 FY26). Growth was volume-led: IP volumes up about 39% and OP up 26%, with occupancy at 65% and ALOS at 2.7 days. Sahyadri (acquired, about 6-7 months in) grew revenue 13% to INR332 crores with EBITDA margin near 17.5%, while ex-Sahyadri margin was 25% versus 26.5% a year earlier, which management attributed to greenfield ramp-up and one-offs. Management also announced the Kinder Hospital (Whitefield, Bangalore, 100 beds) acquisition and reiterated bed additions and capex.

segments.name: Centres of Excellence (6 high-acuity specialties)
segments.commentary: Cardiac Sciences, Oncology, Neurology, Gastroenterology, Orthopaedics and Renal Sciences rose to about 65% of Q1 revenue, with IP revenue in these specialties up 45%. Oncology share grew from 10.8% to 12.2% at network level.

segments.name: Sahyadri Hospitals (9 hospitals, Pune)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR332 crores (up over 13%), EBITDA INR58 crores (up about 19%), margin about 17-17.5%. Integration is planned over 16-18 months; full rebranding to Manipal expected in about 14-16 months from integration.

segments.name: East region (AMRI, Medica, Columbia Asia)
segments.commentary: Top line grew 17% in the quarter, with cash and TPA business up 22% while government business was flat. AMRI grew 17% and Medica 15%.

segments.name: Greenfield hospitals
segments.commentary: Kanakapura broke even at EBITDA in month 5 and Yelahanka in month 2. Two older Bangalore greenfields are at about 13% margin in Q1, ahead of plan.

guidance_outlook: No specific numeric guidance; management said Q1 trends are secular tailwinds, not one-offs, but declined to guide to a core growth number.
Sahyadri margin expected to move closer to the portfolio over the next few quarters; management declined to give a target number or timeline.

Bed additions: Electronic City (about 300 beds) in Q2 FY27; Raipur in Q4 FY27; Nashik added 103 beds in Q1; Kinder (100 beds) possibly accelerated into FY27 as additional beds; Ahilya Nagar about 80 beds in FY28.
Capex: about INR2,000 crores in FY27, with about INR900 crores already spent in Q1; about INR4,000 crores over the next 3-4 years for about 3,000 beds.
Leverage comfort range of 1.5-2x net debt to EBITDA; debt repayment planned in Q2 FY27 from IPO proceeds.
capex_capacity: Bed count over 13,000; 50th hospital (Electronic City, Bangalore, about 300 beds) launched in July 2026, taking Bangalore to about 3,000 licensed beds across 13 facilities.

Kinder Hospital (Whitefield, Bangalore) acquisition of 100 beds including land and building; expected transfer within about 60 days after CPs; to be closed for 6-7 months for remodelling into multispecialty.
Raipur greenfield due Q4 FY27; Juhu (Mumbai) next; Wakad (Pune) greenfield started; Sahyadri expansions at Deccan Gymkhana (new tower), Hadapsar and Nashik oncology capacity (100-plus beds).
New equipment: AI-assisted neuro biplane cath lab at Mukundapur (Kolkata); OCT at MHB Old Airport Road and two other Bangalore sites; Dhakuria (Kolkata) extra beds due next quarter.
demand_pricing: Volume-led growth: IP volumes up about 39% and OP volumes up 26% YoY; management stressed volume over price-led ARPOB growth.
Ex-Sahyadri ARPOB INR77,200/day (up about 9%); Sahyadri ARPOB about INR45,000/day (up 15%).

Scheme collections (government schemes) were slow in Q1, which management said is a sector-wide issue; government mix in East is shifting as a national scheme replaces current schemes, with the authority discussion expected to conclude shortly.
International patients grew about 55% YoY but remain about 3% of revenue; government payers about 14% of institutional mix.
CONGO-R mix about 65% for the network and growing about 45%; complexity mix at Sahyadri is similar to Manipal network.

qa_highlights.question: How will Sahyadri's margin close the gap to corporate average and over what period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sahyadri reached about 17.5% EBITDA margin in Q1 on volume and clinical enhancement, with integration over 16-18 months. No numeric target or timeline was given for reaching network margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ex-Sahyadri margin outlook and the greenfield drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-Sahyadri margin was 25% vs 26.5% last year; management cited about 0.6pp from a one-off Q1 FY26 reversal of INR15 crores, about 0.5pp from fully staffed greenfield doctor costs, and slower scheme collections. Greenfields are expected to ramp up.

qa_highlights.question: Is core standalone growth sustainable beyond Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 trends are not one-offs and called them secular tailwinds from volume growth, high-acuity specialties, and greenfield ramp-up, without guiding to a specific core growth figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kinder acquisition's margin and rationale given its small size?
qa_highlights.answer: Current Kinder revenue is about INR3-4 crores per month (about INR22 crores run-rate); management said the current EBITDA is irrelevant as the asset will be remodelled into multispecialty, with radiation oncology and transplants excluded. Rationale is adding capacity in the Whitefield micro-market.

qa_highlights.question: What capex and leverage should be assumed for the next few years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR2,000 crores (INR900 crores spent in Q1); about INR4,000 crores over 3-4 years for 3,000 beds. Net debt/EBITDA about 2.8x now, falling to about 0.9x after Q2 debt repayment; comfort range 1.5-2x.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans to move medical colleges into the listed entity?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the listed company will remain a specialty tertiary and quaternary hospital provider and will not dilute that focus.

544851|2026-06.headline: MV Electrosystems expects propulsion output to ramp from 10 units in September to about 40 per month by January, against an order book of 564 propulsion systems worth about INR989 crores.
544851|2026-06.overview: This was the first investor call after the company's listing, with no reported financials in the transcript. Management said deliveries have been limited to 2 or 3 small batches so far, with none in the prior two months, and that IPO proceeds (working capital) now fund a scale-up. Management targets about INR400 crore of revenue this year and roughly 10% PAT once run-rate is reached, though it conceded margins are negative or constrained during the initial ramp. Growth optionality was discussed across EMU/MEMU/Vande Bharat distributed propulsion, OHE auto fault locators (with PNC Technologies), and marine/electrical adjacencies.

financial_highlights.value: INR1.67 crore (AMC roughly matches this figure over 3 years)

financial_highlights.metric: Working capital requirement at ~INR1,000 crore turnover

financial_highlights.value: 105 days stated in prospectus; last three cycles completed in 85 days

segments.name: Locomotive propulsion systems
segments.commentary: Order book of 564 units valued at about INR989 crore; ramp planned at 10 units in September, 25 in November, 40 per month by January. Capacity built for 55 per month, with 40 chosen as the stable target.

segments.name: EMU/MEMU/Vande Bharat distributed propulsion
segments.commentary: INR86 crore MCF EMU development order with 24-month supply window; design and development targeted in 8-10 months, then approval taking about 15-16 months in total. A 12-coach EMU is about INR16 crore and a 16-coach Vande Bharat about INR40 crore including electrics.

segments.name: Overhead electrification (OHE) / AFL
segments.commentary: Auto fault locator tied up with PNC Technologies (South Korea). Management pegged unit prices at INR12 lakh (sectioning/sub-sectioning) to INR36 lakh (substation transformer), roughly INR1 crore of revenue per transformer section, with installations expected over 5-7 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR400 crore, described as achievable definitively.
Monthly run-rate of about 40 propulsion systems from January, implying roughly INR70 crore a month and about 480 units a year.
PAT of 10%-plus expected once run-rate is reached; management expects profitability within 2-3 months and margins to improve month over month after stabilisation.
R&D spend to be 3%-4% of revenue over time; R&D team to be expanded with a new centre ready by Q3.
Approximately 15-16 months to EMU propulsion approval including development.

Unit 2 already set up; box fabrication and assembly to start the following Monday after the call.

Two additional shifts planned in the existing factory, cited as enabling about 4,500 systems.
demand_pricing: Management cited Indian Railways building about 1,600-1,700 locomotives a year, about 15,000 locomotives in service needing rehabilitation, and 300-500 EMUs tendered or to be tendered this year.

Company said it won about 25-26% of tendered locomotive propulsion quantity, with competitors including Siemens, Alstom, ABB, Medha and BHEL. In the last tender, 7 suppliers were awarded small quantities.
Management said margins were very thin across bidders; company was L2 in two tenders and L1 in one. Bulk purchasing (200-300 sets) was cited as offsetting electronics price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the PLW/CLW propulsion tender cancellation affect the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was unaware of any cancellation and noted an active CLW tender for 748 locomotives. Tender-to-order conversion typically takes 45 days, sometimes up to 90.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company meet the December 26 order deadline, and what is the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply obligations extend to March and into next financial year. Output is planned at 10 units in September, 25 in November, and 40 in January; extensions are typically granted for capacity-constrained suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: What margins apply given rising electronics costs and no price-escalation clause?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 10%-plus PAT at full run-rate; early months will have constrained or negative margins. Bulk procurement of 200-300 sets is offsetting global price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement lead times range from 7 days to 6 months, averaging about 45 days. Payments were received within 15 days on all three dispatches. Working capital of about INR200 crore needed for roughly INR1,000 crore turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation per propulsion system?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply price is INR1.67 crore per locomotive propulsion system; AMC over three years roughly matches that figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EMU/MCF approval process and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Three-month validation at the MCF commissioning depot, performance trials on Delhi-Ambala Road, then a four-month trial covering about 30,000 km before approval.

544871|2026-06.headline: Shiprocket Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34% to INR592 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 9x to INR8.9 crore and emerging segment losses narrowing.

Core revenue rose 22% to INR412 crore at a 12.8% adjusted EBITDA margin, up 50 bps YoY. Emerging revenue rose 70% to INR180 crore, and its adjusted EBITDA margin improved from -38% to -24%. Loss before tax narrowed to INR13.7 crore from INR18 crore, and management said the emerging share of revenue reached 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core CAC rise to about INR3,600 from INR3,100 a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CAC fluctuates with experiments across channels and reactivation, has held steady for years, and is not seasonal. It said the focus is break-even, with CAC of about INR3,000 recovering margin quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Are 3PLs moving into D2C and SMB, and does that threaten Shiprocket?

544880|2026-06.headline: Horizon Industrial Parks Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR200 crores, with EBITDA of INR161 crores (80% margin) and a net loss of INR12 crores.
544880|2026-06.overview: Management's first earnings call after the August IPO, which raised INR4,250 crores of primary capital used for deleveraging to a proforma net debt of about INR2,500 crores at 30 June. Revenue was INR200 crores (+23% YoY) and EBITDA INR161 crores (+36% YoY). Management steered attention to a proforma cash PAT of INR116 crores, arguing the reported net loss is distorted by non-cash depreciation and pre-deleveraging interest. Leasing was 1.9 million sq ft across 13 transactions, with contracted revenue run rate at about INR967-970 crores.

segments.commentary: 17 assets across 7 cities, about 6-7 mn sq ft; rentals about 2.5-3x big-format; yield on cost 13-14% after CWC revenue share. Three mid-mile assets fully leased at INR65-70 per sq ft (as stated). First Pune (Pimpri) delivery targeted Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Does 25% volume growth plus 5% escalation imply about 30% revenue CAGR over 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described four growth engines: contractual escalations plus re-leasing spreads on 29.5 mn sq ft, 6 mn sq ft of large-park development, in-city expansion of about 2 mn sq ft a year, and value-added services at 5-10% of revenue. It did not confirm a 30% CAGR figure.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR967 crore contracted run rate translate into reported EBITDA and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80-85% sits on existing assets with nearly full 12-month revenue flow expected; the 2.4 mn sq ft pre-leased, under-construction area should contribute within 9-12 months. Further 4-4.5 mn sq ft of leases are expected over 9 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for leverage, capex and cost of debt?

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand beyond its 10 markets and pursue acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will explore Tier 1-minus/Tier 2 markets opportunistically (cited Nagpur, Goa, Nashik), focus on share gains in existing Tier 1 markets, and keep acquisitions (land parcels and consolidation of sub-scale platforms) central. No quantified annual addition target was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive intensity in institutional supply?

544880|2026-09.headline: Horizon Industrial Parks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR213 crore, EBITDA INR173 crore at 81% margin, net debt cut to INR2,765 crore.

Net debt fell to INR2,765 crore at September-end from INR4,967 crore at June-end after post-IPO repayments. H1 leasing reached 4.4 million sq ft, about two-thirds of the 6.5 million sq ft FY27 target, and H1 development completions reached 2.7 million sq ft against a 6 million sq ft target. Management said the company is on track for targets and expects the in-city Pune asset to deliver and sign its first lease this quarter.

rows.why: Operational area rose from 28.5 mn sq ft (March 2026) to about 31.5 mn sq ft at Q2, with 2.7 mn sq ft completed in H1 and guidance of nearly 35 mn sq ft by year-end FY27 (about 11% more), and the 6 mn sq ft FY27 target is firmly committed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 leasing of 4.4 mn sq ft (27 transactions) is about two-thirds of the 6.5 mn sq ft FY27 target, contracted revenue crossed INR1,004 crore, and a couple of mn sq ft of pre-commitments are to be delivered over the next 3-4 quarters, though Q3 is seasonally slower.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Land bank for 29-30 mn sq ft is fully paid with construction financing largely in place, speculative build is about two-thirds of the 6 mn sq ft target, and the acquisition engine is guided to restart in the next one to two quarters; utilisation is 94%, well above the 80% threshold.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated the 6.5 mn sq ft leasing target with 4.4 mn sq ft (about two-thirds) done in H1, but flagged Q3 seasonality from festivals and the mid-December to early-January shutdown, so no upgrade was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Stabilised occupancy slipped to 94% from about 95%, Q3 leasing is seasonally slower, 0.7-0.8 mn sq ft of expiries land in H2 FY27, and the in-city Pune first lease and deliveries (Q4 FY27 / Q1 CY27) depend on execution and the CWC litigation remains sub judice.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First multi-story in-city Pune asset is due to deliver by Q4 FY27 / Q1 CY27 with first in-city lease targeted for Q3 FY27 at guided rents of INR60-90/sq ft (2-3x big-format parks), but the tenant and rent are confidential and in-city revenue is negligible today.

rows.label: Interest cost savings from post-IPO debt repayment
rows.why: About INR4,000 crore of debt was repaid at end-Q2, net debt fell to INR2,765 crore from INR4,967 crore, and cost of debt is about 8.2%, with the benefit guided to show mainly from Q3 and H1 impact negligible.

rows.label: Rooftop solar scale-up
rows.why: About 38 MW is operational or under implementation against a 150-200 MW roof potential, with a planned 10 MW project at INR42-43 crore, but management said regulatory open-access approval is needed and gave no timeline.

rows.label: CWC litigation outcome
rows.why: The matter remains sub judice with no hearing since Jan 2026; the court will not stop development in the interim, so the outcome is uncertain and could affect the in-city pipeline.

tone.note: Management was confident on leasing momentum, the 6 mn sq ft completion target and balance-sheet repair, but guarded on litigation, in-city rents (confidential) and solar scale; analysts pushed on the Q2 growth split and the occupancy dip to 94%.

544882|2026-06.headline: Shankesh Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR424 crore and PAT to INR43 crore, but management gave few numbers to explain the margin jump.

Revenue from operations was INR424 crore (up 55% YoY from INR273 crore), gross profit INR66 crore, EBITDA INR61 crore and PAT INR43 crore. Management attributed growth to customer relationships and product mix, while stating volumes were roughly flat YoY. Analysts repeatedly pressed for quantified margin bridges, volume data and gold-inventory gains; management mostly answered qualitatively and offered to provide more detail later.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 55% YoY growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were approximately the same YoY, so growth came from product mix and customer relationships. No quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin, given EBITDA of about 14% in Q1 after 9.5% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins move quarter to quarter with product mix and that the company focuses on profit amount rather than percentage. It did not commit to a sustainable margin range.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price risk hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: The company buys gold equal to what it sells on the same day at market price. Inventory is carried at a weighted-average cost that management says is below market, so no hedging is needed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion comes from product mix and how much from inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix was one factor and gold-price gains add 1-3 percentage points YoY. Analysts disputed that Q1 had gold gains, and management gave no split.

qa_highlights.question: How is growth funded and what is the working-capital cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Profits are reinvested, and the bank lines are open. The IPO raised equity to about INR450 crore to fund working capital. Management said the business needs more working capital as it grows.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers moving karigar work in-house, and what is the moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said handcrafted, co-created bridal designs and long-standing relationships protect the business. It gave no figures to show the moat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did job-worker count fall and employee cost drop QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers larger, organised contract manufacturers. Employee cost fell because Q4 included an ex-gratia payment to directors, which will not recur.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14% vs 9.5% in Q4 FY26; management gave no sustainable range and said margins move with product mix. Track next quarter's gross and EBITDA margin against this base.

Unquantified growth drivers: 55% revenue growth attributed to mix and relationships with volumes described only as 'approximately same'; volume split and gold-price contribution (management cited 1-3 pp YoY) were not quantified. Watch for the promised Q2/Q3 volume data.

Working capital and funding: trade receivables of INR126 crore (about 22-23 days), inventory turnover about 8x, and management saying working capital needs keep growing; IPO proceeds (INR38 crore working-capital portion) are a key use to track against bank line usage.

Customer in-housing and moat: analysts questioned whether large customers such as Kalyan and P.N. Gadgil moving to in-house karigars threatens the outsourced model; management gave no share or retention figures.

Gold-price hedging and inventory accounting: hedging relies on a same-day buy-to-sell policy and weighted-average inventory valued below market; management did not show the inventory gain component, which analysts disputed for Q1.

544885|2026-06.headline: Gaja AMC Q1 FY27 PAT rose 35% YoY to INR27.2 crores; total income up 26% to INR51.8 crores.
544885|2026-06.overview: First quarterly call as a listed company. Total income rose 26% YoY to INR51.8 crores and PAT rose 35% to INR27.2 crores, with LTM PAT at INR89.1 crores (+38%). Performance income of INR29.7 crores (+17% YoY) drove most of the income, while management fee income of about INR16 crores grew 7%. Cost-to-income improved to 38.4% from 42.3%. Management repeatedly declined to give forward guidance on carry, fund deployment or fundraising timelines.

segments.commentary: About INR16 crores in Q1 FY27, up 7% YoY. Management fee is charged on initial committed capital of Funds III and IV, roughly INR3,200 crores, not on AUM.

segments.commentary: INR29.7 crores in Q1 FY27, up 17% YoY; LTM INR92.2 crores (INR72 crores sponsor gains and INR20 crores carry per the LTM split given on the call). Carry is booked on a realised basis only. Q1 carry of INR13 crores came from Fund II.

guidance_outlook: Management has a stated policy of not giving future guidance on carry, fund wind-up, deployment or fundraising timelines.
Fund V (flagship) targets INR2,500 crores over a 10-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received. Management said the size may increase a bit.
Eastgate (secondaries) targets INR1,500 crores over a 5-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received.
Historical trendlines cited: profit about 35% CAGR (Mar-24 to Mar-26) and total income about 24% a year. Not presented as guidance.
Dividend of INR0.75 per share (15%); payout ratio raised to 12.5% from about 10%.
PW (PricewaterhouseCoopers) to be appointed statutory auditor, replacing the previous auditor.

Eastgate (secondaries): seeking INR1,500 crores over a 5-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received; provides liquidity to Indian PE/VC managers via portfolio stake acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Fund IV dry powder and number of targeted investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 10-12 investments per fund; seven made in Fund IV by June 2026, deployment at 75% rising to 81% since. Fund V will also target 10-12 investments.

qa_highlights.question: Share of carry vs fee income and whether pure fee income will grow faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said performance income becomes more predictable as firms mature, and that fee income does not grow with NAV. Q1 split was about INR16 crores fee and INR30 crores performance; LTM is the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of performance income into carry and sponsor gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: INR13 crores carry from Fund II and INR17 crores sponsor gains from Funds III and IV, total INR29.7 crores. LTM performance income INR92.2 crores (INR72 crores sponsor gains, INR20 crores carry). Carry is booked on realised basis.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Fund III carry given low gross IRR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to say; NAVs are carried conservatively and it expects Fund III performance income trends to continue, with sponsor gains already flowing.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 to Q1 jump of about 594% in carry fee; is it realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 FY26 weakness to low markets and multiple re-rating in March 2026. The Q1 jump reflects fair value gains from the recovery in markets through June, not realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to AI deals such as Fractal and Sarvam and entry valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to discuss underlying fund investments in detail. Said both are mature growth-stage deals, not venture; sector exposure capped at 20-25% of fund capital.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost rise from Q4 to Q1 (INR6.7 crores to INR10.3 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 has seasonal bonus payouts; YoY, Q1 employee costs are in the same range of INR10-plus crores.

qa_highlights.question: Market value of portfolio and LP share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no single portfolio; valuations are done quarterly under SEBI rules and the same valuations are used for the company's holdings.

qa_highlights.question: Fund III and Fund V, Eastgate timelines and first closes?
qa_highlights.answer: Declined to give future guidance on wind-up, deployment or fundraising timing.

544886|2026-06.headline: Tempsens Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% to INR118 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 22% from 25.3% on higher employee cost.
544886|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 33% YoY to INR118 crores, led by Electrical Heating (+148.8% to INR25 crores) and Temperature Sensing (+42% to INR60 crores), while Specialized Cables fell 8.8% to INR32.5 crores on export order timing. EBITDA rose 15.7% to INR26.6 crores, but margin compressed about 330 bps to 22%, driven by a roughly 140 bps hit from employee cost (up 45% to INR20.4 crores) and a high prior-year gross margin base. Management guided FY27 revenue growth in line with the three-year blended growth rate and said margins should recover in H2 FY27. Four capacity projects with aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores are slated to commission between Q4 FY27 and Q3 FY28.

segments.name: Temperature Sensing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR60 crores, up 42%, led by thermal power and OEMs including CVD equipment makers; EDGE pyrometer series (with Micro-Epsilon) to start dispatch in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Electrical Heating
segments.commentary: Revenue INR25 crores, up 148.8% on oil and gas dispatches in India, Southeast Asia and Middle East; 5-year standard furnace supply contract signed with a life sciences OEM.

segments.name: Specialized Cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crores, down 8.8% on export order timing; cable harness line launched with UL certification; Unit 8 greenfield under construction, completion by Q2 FY28.

EBITDA margin to remain broadly similar to FY26 profile; margin recovery visible in H2 FY27 as employee cost is absorbed by revenue.
Management expects profit growth to be in line with revenue growth by end of FY27.

OEM and new products expected to contribute more than 25% of revenue starting FY28.

Unit 8 greenfield cable plant, completion by Q2 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR60 crores; capacity can be ramped quickly.
Victura JV to acquire 80,000 sq ft facility with existing shed; production to start by Q4 FY27, peak revenue potential about INR120 crores.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said field trials and run-up are advanced and focus is now on scaling execution; it declined to quantify exit run-rate, calling it a work in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from critical, high-barrier industries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated roughly 75-90% of revenue from critical applications, with 10-20% from regular, more competitive industries; vendor approvals can take 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the new-age industry TAM and its contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify TAM; said new-age products could grow in the high 20s or 30s percent over 2-3 years. Newer products segment addressable market is about INR3,000 crores with less than 1% currently addressed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin recovery bridge and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost increase reflects headcount added for future projects; margin recovery expected to start in H2 FY27, not FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Middle East/Africa and political situation a risk to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no negative impact seen in the next few quarters; electrification trend could be positive mid-term.

qa_highlights.answer: Capacity comes online from Q1 FY28 with construction largely done by Q3 FY28; full utilisation expected around FY29-FY30, with plants typically run at about 80% maximum.
