qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and capacity expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: INR30 crore capex this year, to be implemented within one year. A 6.5-acre land purchase is planned for a future plant estimated at INR350–500 crore in 2–3 years; a US subsidiary is also being set up.

qa_highlights.question: How is the US business and export mix planned?
qa_highlights.answer: US is about 25% of revenue and management intends to hold it there. Total export target is 50% in five years, spread across Europe, Australia, New Zealand and Dubai.

qa_highlights.question: Why did new SKU additions fall from about 2,206 in FY24 to about 880 in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SKU additions depend on OEM RFQs for new equipment, not on cost or a deliberate slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said absolute employee cost rose in line with the top line, and that a cut-off sales shift into Q2 makes the ratio about 12% of sales.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 must show the OEM price pass-through and margin recovery toward 24–25%; the Q1 margin fall (19.6% vs 21.5%) is the key open point.
Dependence on US exports (about 25% of revenue) under tariff and geopolitical risk; management says it will cap US share.
Execution of the INR30 crore capex and the 6.5-acre plant (INR350–500 crore), including land acquisition in 3–4 months and government approvals.
Railway (IRIS), defence (DRDO) and shipyard (Cochin Shipyard, Mazagon Dock) orders are at registration stage; first revenue is uncertain, possibly after 5–6 months.

544898|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 7.28% YoY to INR 133.66 crore and PAT grew 14% to INR 29.28 crore, while growth depends on GPU capacity going live from Q3.
544898|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 133.66 crore, up 7.28% YoY but down 20.20% QoQ, which management attributed to design services booked in a subsidiary (SPOCHUB) in Q4 FY26. PAT rose about 14% to INR 29.28 crore and EBITDA was INR 559 million at a stated 42% margin. Management said the step-up depends on the Sharon AI GPU deal (8,200 B300 GPUs in Sydney), now expected to bill from Q3 FY27 after a delay from the earlier mid-September target. Management declined to give any forward revenue or profit guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Sharon AI go-live delayed from mid-September, and when will revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the date slipped by about 1.5 months, with billing starting now. It targets early Q3 or mid-Q3, and later said November first week go-live, with billing from Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the quarterly revenue growth (7-8%) inconsistent with a 30-40% order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality with Q3 and Q4 stronger historically; Q1 growth of about 8% was called appropriate given domestic deliverables. Growth is expected QoQ from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GPU pricing locked for the Sharon deal and can its rate be fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the Sharon GPU purchase cost and the customer revenue are both locked at pre-decided rates, with a 7-year contract.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1,500 GPUs be deployed by Q4 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the target as correct, with deployment by January-February 2027 (mid-to-end Q4).

qa_highlights.question: Are there capex subsidies (PLI) or any client concentration risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not eligible for capex subsidies such as PLI. On concentration, management said advance-funded contracts reduce risk, and it did not name the clients or confirm any China exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be any deal-related guidance for FY27 or FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management declined to provide forward-looking revenue or profit figures.

544901|2026-06.headline: Purple Style Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR119 crores (from INR106 crores), but EBITDA was negative INR11 crores vs negative INR4 crores a year earlier.
544901|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with the four large-format experience centres opened in FY26 (Fort Mumbai, South Ex Delhi, Linking Road Bandra, Madison Avenue New York). GMV rose to INR193 crores from INR133 crores and AOV rose to INR86,000 from INR66,000. Revenue from operations was INR119 crores, gross margin held at 36%, and EBITDA and PAT losses were wider than a year earlier on the higher fixed cost base of the new stores. Inventory and net working capital fell year on year, but borrowings rose to INR436 crores at June 2026 from INR371 crores at FY26 end.

segments.name: Mumbai (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR50 crores from INR28 crores in the first three months of FY26. Mumbai was the largest market in FY26 GMV at INR205 crores.

segments.name: Delhi (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR39 crores from INR29 crores. Delhi FY26 GMV was INR166 crores.

segments.name: Hyderabad (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR16 crores from INR10 crores.

segments.name: USA (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR29 crores from INR20 crores. New York flagship opened in March 2026 and is the first US store; US was online-only before that.

guidance_outlook: No objective margin or profitability guidance given; management said it would refrain from it.
Q1 is the leanest quarter; management said the cost structure set in Q1 will carry into Q2 absent changes, and clearer trends are expected over the next two quarters.
No significant new experience centre expansion is planned near term; the first full year of the FY26 store investments is to be observed.

EBITDA break-even framing: on a P&L basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed for zero EBITDA, with lease-related costs of INR45 crores (lease interest plus ROU depreciation) included. On a cash basis, lease payments of INR29 crores imply a smaller gap.
Lease interest and ROU depreciation are expected to stay broadly flat unless stores change. Other finance cost should decline as operating profit reduces debt.
capex_capacity: Four large-format experience centres opened in FY26: Fort Mumbai and South Ex Delhi (operational since Q2 FY26), Linking Road Bandra (end-March 2026), and Madison Avenue New York (March 2026).
Store footprint is organised by geography, not by store, so same-store sales are not tracked. Mumbai now runs two large-format centres.
The New York lease is a June-end lease with a shorter tenure, so rent can be adjusted after 12-18 months of performance.
Inventory is expected to stay roughly flat at the current level absent further expansion. Management said inventory is around INR160 crores, with breadth-led singular-unit stock.
demand_pricing: AOV rose to INR86,000 in Q1 FY27, from INR76,000 in FY26 and INR46,000 in FY24. Store AOV is about 2.5x online AOV (India online about INR38,000 vs store about INR90,000 in FY26).
Active designer brands fell to 1,109 in FY26 from 1,910 in FY24. Top 100 designers were 67% of sales in FY24.
Average GMV per customer rose to INR108,000 in FY26 from INR67,000 in FY24. Top 50,000 customers contributed INR702 crores of FY26 GMV of INR722 crores.
Women's wear above INR1 lakh grew to INR312 crores GMV in FY26 from INR187 crores in FY24. Women's wear below INR35,000 fell to INR86 crores from INR162 crores.
Gross margin percentage is said to be broadly flat across price points. Management argued that absolute gross profit per piece rises with higher ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow still negative and borrowings rising despite lower inventory and working capital? When does the business become self-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower inventory reflects better inventory management after the FY22-25 build-up, and higher customer advances (INR49 crores) helped working capital. Debt is funding interest costs, and Q1 is not operationally profitable. It asked investors to observe the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the higher-ticket strategy improve gross margin or only AOV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said percentage gross margin is similar across categories. The benefit is in absolute gross profit per piece (e.g., at 40% margin a INR2 lakh piece yields INR80,000 vs INR8,000 for a INR20,000 piece), plus lower supply and customer complexity from the long tail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of outright purchase, consignment and backorder inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consignment split is business-sensitive and not disclosed. Outright purchase forms the inventory on the books. Backorder advances are about one month of revenue, and average delivery is 45-60 days, so backorder customer advances are not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for finance costs in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease interest plus ROU depreciation (INR45 crores in the P&L) should stay at Q1 levels absent new store changes. Other finance cost should fall as operating profit reduces debt.

qa_highlights.question: What GMV scale, gross margin and operating leverage are needed for EBITDA positivity?
qa_highlights.answer: On an EBITDA basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed. Adding the lease costs of INR45 crores (P&L) or INR29 crores (cash) raises the required gross profit. Management referred to the detailed P&L on slide 20.

qa_highlights.question: What is the New York store's AOV and break-even, and what is the SSG for mature stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a New York store AOV of about INR1.25 lakh (about USD1,500), based on a 2.5x multiple to online AOV. It did not give a break-even GMV. Same-store growth is not tracked because the company reports by geography.

544903|2026-09.headline: Deepa Jewellers Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.24% on plain-gold mix and PAT rose 37% to INR 37 crore.
544903|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, with EBITDA of INR 45 crore (up 17% YoY, margin 7.24%) and PAT of INR 37 crore (up 37%, margin 5.96%). H1 FY27 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,057 crore, EBITDA rose 24% to INR 84 crore (7.95% margin) and PAT rose 32% to INR 64 crore. Management attributed the Q2 growth moderation to festive demand shifting into H2, and said lower gross margin came from a plain-gold-heavy sales mix, with PAT supported by other income and a lower tax rate. The company also commenced its in-house Hyderabad manufacturing facility in September 2026 and guided to 40-45% revenue CAGR for FY27-FY29.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Volume of 318 kg in Q2 (+44% YoY) and 544 kg in H1 (+51% YoY). Realisation per gram fell to about INR 178-180 from about INR 200 a year earlier, which management attributed to plain-gold mix rather than pricing changes.

segments.name: Jewellery manufacturing (invoice/own gold)
segments.commentary: Volume of 491 kg in Q2 (broadly stable) and 783 kg in H1 (-5% YoY). Own-processing realisation fell to about INR 12,600/g from INR 14,500/g, attributed to lower gold prices, plain-gold mix and higher 18-karat sales.

segments.name: Studded vs plain gold mix
segments.commentary: Studded share was 57% of H1 FY27 sales, against 65% in FY26, with plain gold at 43%. Management targets studded share of 75% over the next three to four quarters.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 40-45% guided for FY27, FY28 and FY29, with FY27 growth of 40-45% compared with FY26 (March 2026) base; the 40-45% figure was also described as a 40-50% revenue CAGR for two years at a constant 24-karat gold rate of INR 50,000.
EBITDA margin expected to expand 80-120 bps over the next 4-6 quarters, driven by the Hyderabad facility, Tier-2/3 expansion, studded mix and standalone store sales.
Gross margin pressure from plain-gold mix expected to normalise in upcoming quarters.
Hedging to rise from 94% toward close to 100% of gold holdings over the next two to three quarters.
Working capital cycle (inventory days plus receivable days) expected in the 55-65 day range; inventory and receivables expected to normalise from Q3.
Internal accruals, IPO proceeds and existing debt expected to fund growth through FY29.
Effective tax rate guided at the standard 25.168%; Q2 benefit came from deferred tax on IPO expenses, with the tax shield reversing in later years.
capex_capacity: In-house manufacturing facility in Hyderabad, about 6,700 sq ft, commenced operations in September 2026.
Facility capacity of about 1.5 tonnes a year on single shift and about 2.5 tonnes a year on double shift.
Facility processed 65 kg (13% of volume) in Q1 FY27 and 167 kg (21%) in Q2 FY27; management expects about 40% in Q3 and about 50% in Q4.
Second sales office in Chennai planned for December 2026; Bangalore office planned for April-May 2027, following Vijayawada office.
Long-run target mix of 65% in-house and 35% outsourced manufacturing; outsourced work to shift in-house from Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Revenue concentrated in South India (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala); client base about 373 customers including 47 jewellery retail chains such as Joyalukkas, Kalyan, Lalitha and Bhima.
Q2 growth moderated as festive demand shifted into H2; H1 typically contributes about 40% of annual revenue.
Retail customers shifting from cash purchases to old-gold exchange after a gold price spike, moving sales from invoice basis to job work; management said total volume shifted rather than fell.

Job work conversion margin is about 75% and invoice-basis about 8%, with a similar ROCE/ROE in both models; job work is priced at about 1% lower wastage (4% vs 5%) because it needs no working capital.
Gold price assumption for guidance: constant 24-karat rate of INR 50,000 per 10 g; average selling gold price rose from about INR 8,000/g in FY25 to INR 11,950/g in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin and grammage realisation decline in Q2, and why did job work realisation drop about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change was a shift toward plain gold jewellery (lower margin than studded), not a strategic or operational change, and expects normalisation. Job work realisation fell to about INR 178 from INR 202 a year earlier (about 11%), attributed to the same SKU mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and receivable days rise versus March 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March is not a like-for-like base because year-end corporate purchases stop; higher inventory came from stock built for the new Vijayawada sales office in September after IPO proceeds. Management expects normalisation from Q3 and a combined inventory plus receivable cycle of 55-65 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue outlook for the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth to come from new geographies (Vijayawada, Chennai, Bangalore offices), SKU expansion into studded casting, Nakshi and Tapa jewellery (16 SKUs launched in Q1), and client store expansion including franchise models. Guidance is 40-45% CAGR for FY27-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of the new facility, and what EBITDA margin should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation and karigar costs weighed on Q1 and Q2 margins; benefit expected from Q3 as more volume shifts in-house. Management guided to an 80-120 bps EBITDA margin expansion over 4-6 quarters, with a note that studded mix and standalone store sales also contribute.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price exposure hedged, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: 94% of gold holdings were hedged as of 30 September through gold metal loans (3.25% p.a.), MCX short futures and back-to-back unfixed purchases from bullion suppliers. Target is close to 100% within two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate fall to about 15%, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the standard rate is 25.168%; the lower Q2 rate reflects deferred tax on IPO expenses, which Companies Act treats against securities premium while Income Tax allows over five years. The effect is expected to even out in later years.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters draw salary, and how will they be compensated?
qa_highlights.answer: Both Ashish Agarwal and Dev Agarwal will not draw salary from 1 October 2026, and Dev Agarwal said no salary is planned for at least 10 quarters, after which the board will decide.

Shift of retail customers toward old-gold exchange could keep invoice-basis sales subdued and raise job work share.
Customer concentration in South India and in a few large jewellery chains.
Tax rate normalisation from Q2 deferred benefit back to 25.168%.
Hedging coverage to rise to close to 100%; monitor in next quarter.

Management was more evasive on specifics, notably the EBITDA margin direction (a live misstatement of 80-120 bps versus a dip was clarified on the call) and on the basis for the 40-45% CAGR. 544911|2026-06.headline: Kanohar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 103.5% YoY to INR137.1 crore, with EBITDA margin of 28.3% and order book of about INR2,026 crore.
544911|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR137.1 crore, up 103.5% YoY, with transformers at 84.9% and EPC at 14.81% of revenue. EBITDA rose 152.2% to INR38.8 crore (28.3% margin, up 550 bps) and PAT rose 140% to INR27.3 crore (19.9% margin). Consolidated order book stood at about INR2,026 crore on June 30, 2026, up 11% from March 31, 2026, after incremental orders of INR332.2 crore in Q1 and INR867.3 crore in Q2 to date. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR950 crore with EBITDA margin similar to FY26, with H2 as the main execution period.

financial_highlights.value: Q1: INR332.2 crore; Q2 to date: INR867.3 crore

segments.name: Power Transformers / 400 kV
segments.commentary: 400 kV transformers contributed 70.16% of Q1 revenue (52% in FY26, 10.3% in FY24). Management said 400 kV, Scott-connected and shunt reactor products carry similar gross margins; about 70% of order book is power transformers, mostly 400 kV.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: EPC contributed 14.81% of Q1 revenue. Management does not disclose EBITDA separately; directionally lower than transformer margins.

segments.commentary: Power Transmission 85.18%, Railways 11.53%, Renewable Energy 2.84%, Power Distribution 0.23% of Q1 revenue. Shunt reactors were about 13.1% of order book at June 30.

segments.commentary: 132 kV to below 220 kV at 11.38%, 220 kV to below 400 kV at 3.19%, below 132 kV at 0.23% of Q1 revenue.

Brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol, targeted to be in place by end-FY28 / FY29; existing capacity seen sufficient through FY28.
Net working capital guided at 110-120 days.

Shunt reactors expected to be about 10-15% of revenue on average over time.

About 2,500 kW solar plant planned, partly funded from IPO proceeds; savings not quantified.

Railways envisages about 1,000 traction substations for high-speed rail over 5-10 years (about 2,000 transformers), implying about INR20,000 crore opportunity.
Most contracts have price variation clauses (IEEMA PVC), which management says offsets raw material swings; order book margins said to be similar to FY26.

Management said there were no new entrants in the last 3-6 months that it is aware of, but expects new entrants over time.

qa_highlights.question: How were transformer margins protected in Q1 given input cost increases and fixed-price contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most contracts carry price variation linked to the IEEMA clause, which passes through raw material moves in both directions.

qa_highlights.question: Will GEC-III drive a multi-year order tailwind for 400 kV and 500 MVA transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a multi-decadal structural tailwind; intra-state transmission is mostly 400 kV, but no split of GEC-III capacity by voltage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can order book reach INR3,000 crore by FY27 end, and 40-45% YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to confirm; said Q2 execution will reduce the order book slightly, and end-FY27 book may cover FY28-FY29 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1H-weak, 2H-heavy revenue pattern a continuing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said H1 is typically softer and H2 heavier, an industry trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will new 400 kV capacity pressure margins beyond 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visibility for 3-4 years from current order book and tenders; beyond that, short-term supply-demand mismatch and margin pressure are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY24 a revenue decline and why is utilisation low; are exports planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY24 focus went to obtaining 400 kV and Scott certifications; ramp-up takes time. Exports are not the current focus; a re-look may come in 3-4 years.

544912|2026-06.headline: Prasol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.7% YoY to INR433.6 crores and EBITDA to INR90.3 crores, helped by one-off inventory gains of about INR25 crores.
544912|2026-06.overview: First earnings call after the 16 September 2026 listing. Revenue from operations was INR433.6 crores (up 35.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin of 20.8% and PAT of INR61 crores (14.1% margin). Management attributed about INR25 crores of gross profit to a sharp rise in selling prices from West Asia-linked supply disruptions and inventory bought at lower prices, which it called partly non-structural. FY27 guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores revenue and INR240-250 crores adjusted EBITDA excludes these gains, and management described a 15-16% year-end EBITDA margin. A Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores for existing products (about 60,000 tpa of added capacity) was outlined.

segments.commentary: About 40% of Q1 FY27 revenue; described as the fastest-growing category, about 38% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Other specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Balance about 20% of Q1 revenue; customised products built around specific customer needs.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 27% of Q1 FY27 revenue, stated as stable or growing despite West Asia disruption to Dubai and Africa shipments.

segments.name: Mahad plant
segments.commentary: About 19,900 tpa capacity; utilisation rose from about 13% in FY24 to 44% in FY26, and management says it was EBITDA and PBT positive in Q1 (about 60% utilisation cited).

Management says export volumes to Europe were rising to offset weaker shipments to Africa and the Middle East, and that the West Asia war cost up to about 10% of potential export growth.

REACH registration for six or seven products; mining chemicals approved in US, with commercial volumes expected in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the acetone sourcing diversification need storage or logistics investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR25 crores is set aside for a floating-roof storage tank and more than INR25 crores will go into adjoining Khopoli land over the next year, with barge-based shipping expected to cut transport costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EBITDA guidance (INR240-250 crores) only modestly above the Q1 run-rate?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Mahad outlook and how much EBITDA did it contribute in Q1?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said stock is built from January-February for the April season, with raw materials bought at pre-war prices, and that it does not speculate on raw material prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for additional capex for the R&D pipeline, and on what land?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15-20% of about 40 pipeline products typically get commercialised; the newer chemistry will use the land already bought, and environmental clearance for one or two products is in an advanced stage (9-12 months typical).

544913|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to Rs.107 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to Rs.23 crore, with margin at 21.3% and a Rs.982 crore order book.
544913|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs.107 crore, up 36% YoY, led by domestic facade (Rs.62 crore, +93%) and fenestration (Rs.6 crore, +127%), while international fell 12% to Rs.39 crore on delivery timing. EBITDA grew 9% to Rs.23 crore, and margin fell to 21.3% because of lower international contribution and a shift to DDP freight billing at cost. Management attributed about 1.5 points of the margin gap to freight pass-through and said the underlying margin is in line with FY26. PAT of Rs.17 crore grew more slowly than EBITDA due to lower other income (prior-year property sale gain) and higher depreciation from new capacity. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 25% revenue growth, 23-25% EBITDA margin and 18-20% PAT margin, while flagging a weak first half and a heavier Q3 and Q4.

financial_highlights.change: Lower YoY; international margin cited at 36.3%
Grew slower than EBITDA; lower other income and higher depreciation

segments.name: Domestic facade (turnkey, Grade A developers)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.62 crore, up 93% YoY; all order book is commercial real estate in Tier 1 cities. Historically about 49% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: International facade (B2B product supply, US and Australia)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.39 crore, down 12% YoY on delivery timing; management expects Q3 and Q4 to be stronger with three projects. Historically about 45% of FY26 revenue; FY26 Australia revenue was Rs.24 crore.

segments.name: Fenestration (luxury doors and windows)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.6 crore, up 127% YoY on luxury residential demand. Historically about 6% of FY26 revenue. Higher margin, lower volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 25% YoY (management also cited a 20-25% CAGR ambition).
FY27 EBITDA margin of 23-25% and PAT margin of 18-20% on a consolidated basis, with freight pass-through expected to have limited impact.
Revenue mix for FY27 to stay similar to FY26 (about 49% domestic, 45% international, 6% fenestration).
Glass processing unit commissioning expected in about 8 months, with an estimated 1-1.5% EBITDA margin benefit.
Target of at least 2 years of order book visibility.
capex_capacity: Vile Bhagad (Mangaon) plant on a 1 lakh sq m owned MIDC plot; about 32,000 sq m built to date and about 30% of land used.
Current capacity about 130 panels a day across four production lines, with about 350 workers (about 120 on payroll).
Glass processing unit under construction; total project cost Rs.80 crore, funded by Rs.50 crore fresh issue and internal accruals; commissioning in about 8 months.
Management says infrastructure supports growth for the next couple of years without incremental capex.
In-house NABL-accredited test facility for air, water, seismic, structural and movement testing.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs.982 crore as on 31 July 2026, with no substantial new orders in the past three months; a few near-closure international jobs in the US, Canada and Israel.
Domestic facade market about Rs.9,000 crore, projected to reach about Rs.14,500 crore by FY30 (about 15.9% CAGR, per management).
Management estimates a 6-7% domestic market share, and says it is the second-largest domestic player by revenue.
Contracts include aluminium and glass pass-through across all verticals; freight now billed at cost under DDP terms.
Payment terms are milestone-based (about 10% advance, about 55-60% on material delivery, balance on installation); export invoicing is at dispatch with 60-day credit.
Management said US tariffs could slow US construction demand, but it views the impact on its business as small.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q1 order inflow, and will the freight change and any Q1 delays affect Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no substantial new order came in over the past three months. Freight of about Rs.5.5 crore is a pass-through, and adjusting for it plus the prior-year property gain, margin is in line with FY26. Export is back-ended, with three projects due in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why has margin risen above pre-COVID levels on lower revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the export and fenestration verticals, a shift from residential to commercial projects with faster realisations, pass-through clauses on aluminium and glass, and consolidation from three factories to one.

qa_highlights.question: What is the glass processing unit timeline and benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is expected in about 8 months, with an estimated 1-1.5% bottom-line margin benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order-book and growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to keep at least 2 years of visibility and grow revenue at 20-25% CAGR; a typical order cycle is 18-24 months (export about 12 months, domestic about 24).

qa_highlights.question: What are the market share and competitive position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates about 6-7% domestic share and says it is second-largest by revenue; its direct competitors are three or four players with revenue around Rs.200 crore.

risks_watch: Seasonality: management said the first two quarters are typically slow, so FY27 delivery depends on the heavier Q3 and Q4.
Order inflow: no substantial new orders in the three months to July, and the company is relying on near-closure international wins.
Freight and duty pass-through: under DDP terms the company bears freight and any tariff changes, and mitigation depends on clients accepting pass-through; management said margin % may dilute.
US demand: management said tariffs could slow US construction demand.
Glass processing unit commissioning in about 8 months; the margin benefit is estimated at 1-1.5%.

544914|2026-06.headline: Steamhouse Q1 FY27 PAT rose 80.25% YoY to INR18.34 crore on 16.7% steam volume growth; EBITDA margin 24.05%.
544914|2026-06.overview: Steamhouse reported record quarterly steam volumes of about 3,05,816 tons, up 16.7% YoY and 11.52% QoQ, with revenue from operations up 13.35% to INR128.62 crore. EBITDA rose 60.08% to INR30.93 crore, lifting margin to 24.05% (up 702 bps), while PAT rose 80.25% to INR18.34 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher volumes, utilisation (41.40% vs 36.06% YoY) and operating leverage, and noted the exit from low-margin coal trading. Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore at FY26 end, with IPO proceeds earmarked for debt reduction and capacity expansion.

segments.name: Steam generation and distribution (own boilers)
segments.commentary: Own-generated steam was 73.7% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management said it will be the source of future growth, with waste-to-energy boilers at Vapi supporting realisation.

segments.name: Steam trading (purchased and resold)
segments.commentary: Traded steam was 22.2% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Coal trading has been discontinued as low-margin; two trading agreements (Dahej SEZ, Haldia) are signed and management declined to split margins between generation and trading.

segments.name: Industrial gases / nitrogen
segments.commentary: PSA-based nitrogen plant of 350 Nm3/hr commissioned at Ankleshwar. Management described it as currently small and plans air separation units for LIN/LOX and other gases.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to take utilisation to 60%-65%; newer boilers expected at about 50% in initial months after commissioning.
Steam volume growth of 5%-10% expected at existing locations; company-level 20%-25% volume growth described as 'very comfortably' achievable with new capacity and demand revival.

EBITDA per ton of about INR1,000 expected to be maintained for next few quarters; Q2 seasonally weaker due to monsoon; full-year performance expected to be at par with or better than Q1 run-rate (management said 'we will try' to sustain growth).
Finance costs expected to moderate in FY27 as IPO proceeds repay high-cost borrowings.
Working capital cycle guided at 35-40 days positive.

Capacity to rise from 345 TPH to approx. 705 TPH; four under-construction projects (Jhagadia, Vapi, Nandesari, AMC Pirana) targeted to go live in FY27; Tarapur 60 TPH by Q4 FY28; IPO-funded Dahej, Ankleshwar and Panoli by Q1 FY29.
Una (Himachal Pradesh) 300 TPH EPC project: expected 8%-10% clear margin per ton, pass-through to customers, no capex; agreement not yet signed.

Ankleshwar nitrogen PSA plant of 350 Nm3/hr commenced; ASU for LIN/LOX under evaluation with build-own-operate partners as an option.
Una EPC: 300 TPH community boiler, project value approx. INR311 crore incl. GST, funded by Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Ltd; 9% revenue share to be recovered from end customers.
Pipeline network above 60 km across seven industrial areas; management estimates adding pipelines costs 10%-20% of existing infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Management attributed volume growth to revival in chemical and pharma demand after weak FY24-FY26; tyre and food processing (Haldia agreement) added as new segments.
Customer contracts tenor 1-10 years with non-exit clauses; fuel cost pass-through predominantly monthly, some quarterly; newer contracts include minimum guaranteed off-take.

Monsoon disrupts operations because fuel is wet and industrial clusters flood; Q2 seasonally weaker.
Realisation per ton improved due to better utilisation and higher waste-to-energy mix at Vapi.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in the business across quarters, and what explains the Q1 volume jump over Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no real consumption seasonality, but monsoon is challenging (wet fuel, flooded industrial clusters). Q1 volume growth was attributed to chemical and pharma demand recovering and repeat customers.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the 345 TPH capacity is contracted, and can customers terminate contracts early?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of the 345 TPH installed capacity is tied up under contracts. Tenure ranges 1 to 10 years with non-exit clauses, and management said customers rarely move to captive boilers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value proposition to win customers from competitors or in-house boilers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is generally no competitor in most geographies. Claimed cost saving versus captive furnace oil, LDO or natural gas is 25% to 35%, while coal-fired large textile users may be only at par.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed to reach 705 TPH and when will projects go live?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crore more for the four under-construction projects, targeted to go live in FY27. Another INR170 crore over 15-18 months for IPO-funded and Tarapur projects; Tarapur 60 TPH by Q4 FY28, Dahej/Ankleshwar/Panoli by Q1 FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is utilisation of 41% consistent with the planned ramp, and where does the company target it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 60%-65% utilisation; newer boilers are expected to run at about 50% in initial months after commissioning. Some capacity is held back for 2-3 years of new demand.

qa_highlights.question: What are receivable days and CFO to EBITDA ratio, and what are the related-party steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing?
qa_highlights.answer: Fortnightly billing with payments typically 7th to 15th day. Operating cash flow was about 1.2 times EBITDA last time, expected to hold or be slightly lower. Steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing for the Sachin location continue for at least the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected on the Una project and what is the revenue-share structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 8%-10% clear margin per ton, passed through to end consumers, with no capex. The 9% revenue share to Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Ltd is to be recovered from steam customers. Agreement not yet signed.

qa_highlights.question: What is a sustainable volume growth rate and can company-level 20%-25% volume growth be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 5%-10% growth at existing locations, with new capacity adding further. CFO said 20%-25% company-level volume growth is achievable 'very comfortably'.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR1,000 EBITDA per ton sustainable, and what about Q2 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA per ton of about INR1,000 is expected to hold for the next few quarters, with Q2 an exception due to monsoon. Structural changes cited: coal purchases moved from credit to cash, solar power installed, inventory optimisation. Full-year to be at par or better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there government interest in community boilers and are more such opportunities in the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to Bulk Drug Park and PM MITRA Park schemes from 2021-22 and a March 2024 CPCB guideline pushing SMEs to common boilers. Gujarat Bulk Drug Park tender is live; PM MITRA and Textile Ministry discussions are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did steam revenue rise 46% when volume rose 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation improved from better utilisation and asset leverage, plus higher waste-to-energy usage at Vapi. Growth also came from chemical and pharma recovery and new tyre and food processing (Haldia) customers.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital guidance and cash purchases?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle guided at 35-40 days positive. Coal was bought on credit until May 2026 and has since moved entirely to cash purchases, which management said lowers fuel cost.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split between own-generated and traded steam, and margin split by business?
qa_highlights.answer: Own-boiler steam was 73.7% of Q1 revenue and traded steam 22.2%. Management declined to split margins between generation and trading, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA CAGR guidance of 30%-35% going to be beaten?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will try to maintain the Q1 growth momentum for the full year on both EBITDA and revenue, but said 'We are not saying that we will maintain'.

risks_watch: Utilisation is still 41.40% versus a 60%-65% target; newer boilers ramp only to about 50% in initial months, so margin expansion depends on execution.
Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore; IPO proceeds are expected to reduce high-cost debt, but the timing and extent of finance-cost moderation need tracking.
Q2 seasonality from monsoon (wet fuel, flooded clusters) is expected to dent EBITDA per ton below INR1,000; watch Q2 FY27 print.
Coal trading exit and undisclosed split of margins between own generation and traded steam (22.2% of revenue) limit visibility into core-segment profitability.
Four under-construction projects (Jhagadia, Vapi, Nandesari, AMC Pirana) must go live in FY27; about INR60 crore capex remains plus INR170 crore for IPO and Tarapur projects.
Una EPC (INR311 crore, 300 TPH) is not yet signed; the 8%-10% per-ton margin is unconfirmed and depends on fuel price pass-through.
Related-party steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing & Printing continue for at least a few quarters; watch the size and terms.
Nitrogen business is small (350 Nm3/hr PSA) and ASU/LIN/LOX plans are under evaluation with no firm capex or partner decision.
key_quotes: So, we feel that the margin levels can be maintained and can be even better going forward.
But yes, we are saying we will try to maintain. We are not saying that we will maintain.
We are a proxy play to chemical industries, and we are seeing benefits out of it.

Answers were detailed on the pipeline and government demand, while the Una agreement and nitrogen plans were left unfinalised.

544914|2026-09.headline: Steamhouse Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.4% to INR128 crore and EBITDA rose 73% YoY to INR24.68 crore, but both fell sequentially from Q1.
544914|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 steam sales were 3,01,642 tons, up 12.06% YoY but down about 1.36% QoQ, with monsoon conditions and one steam supplier's shutdown cited as drags. Revenue from operations was INR128 crore (up 2.4% YoY) and EBITDA was INR24.68 crore, with margin at 19.28% against 11.39% a year earlier. Sequentially, EBITDA fell from INR30.93 crore in Q1 and EBITDA per ton declined, which management attributed to monsoon-related fuel wetness, transmission losses and cost movements. H1 FY27 steam sales rose 14.35% YoY, and management reiterated 25% FY27 volume growth and 35% growth in FY28, with an EBITDA per ton target of INR1,100-1,200 for the next full year.

segments.name: Steam generation and distribution
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue from steam generation and distribution was INR96.97 crore; steam distribution contributed INR25.56 crore. Own generation was 2,31,775.59 tons and steam purchase/distribution was 69,866.67 tons in Q2.

segments.name: Nitrogen and other
segments.commentary: Balance of Q2 revenue (about INR5.5 crore) came from nitrogen and other items; nitrogen is billed per nm3 per hour, not per ton. A 750 nm3/hour PSA plant at Ankleshwar is expected by end-CY2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 steam volume growth target of about 25% over FY26's 10.66 lakh tons, implying about 13.25 lakh tons; H2 must grow about 35% YoY versus H1 to hit this.
FY28 volume growth expected to be upwards of 35%, driven by new facilities and customers added in FY27.
Next full year EBITDA per ton guided at INR1,100-1,200, supported by waste-to-steam facilities; Q3 and Q4 expected to be significantly higher than Q2 as the dry season reduces fuel losses.
Quarterly interest cost guided to be a little below the approx INR6 crore run-rate in Q3, as IPO proceeds repaid part of the debt raised in Q1.
Jhagadia steam sales expected to start in November 2026; Nandesari and Vapi waste-to-steam plants expected in H2 FY27; a third waste-to-steam plant expected in the next calendar year.
capex_capacity: Jhagadia: about 14.8 tons per hour contracted out of 30 tons per hour planned; commissioning expected imminently.

Nandesari and Vapi expansions progressing; Vapi is about 7-8 km from existing facility and includes a roughly 1.5 km pipeline. Tarapur and Pirana under construction (Pirana targeting textile cluster in Ahmedabad).

Una (Himachal Pradesh) community boiler: 300 tons per hour, EPC mandate of about INR311 crore incl. GST plus long-term O&M; funded by Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Limited; pricing still under negotiation.
Waste-to-steam capex is about 1.5x-1.75x coal-fired projects on a like-for-like capacity basis, with opex about 50-55% lower; management cites a 2.5-3.5 year payback after stabilisation.
Capacity utilisation: 42.41% in Q2 FY27 vs 35.28% in Q2 FY26 and 41.40% in Q1 FY27; H1 FY27 at 41.91% vs 37.03%.
demand_pricing: Steam volumes grew 14.35% YoY in H1 FY27 to 6,07,459 tons (5,31,240 tons in H1 FY26); 99.48% of H1 FY27 revenue came from repeat customers.
Steam prices were raised about 17-18% from Q1 to Q2 and the pass-through of coal price changes is contractual, with a lag of around 15 days.
Fuel: imported Indonesian 4,200 GCV coal at about INR10,000-10,500 per ton as of the call, up from INR9,000-10,000 earlier and a temporary INR10,500-11,000 peak at end-September.
New sectors being added include food processing and adhesives, on top of the chemical, agrochemical and pharma base; Narol textile cluster targeted via Pirana.
Management said it is evaluating a large waste-based steam project in Sachin GIDC targeting the textile cluster, which is price sensitive.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth is expected for H2 FY27 and FY28 based on current contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is about 25% volume growth over 10.66 lakh tons in FY26; FY28 volume growth is expected to be upwards of 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton fall from about INR1,000 to about INR818 QoQ, and what is coal cost and interest outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop to monsoon-related wet coal, higher transmission losses and cost movements; coal is a pass-through. Quarterly interest expected to be slightly below about INR6 crore in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA per ton is expected from the Himachal Pradesh (Una) EPC project given the 9% government revenue share and imported coal transport?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing and markup are still under negotiation; margins will be lower than the current model as no capex is on the books, though PBT is expected to be broadly in line.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% volume growth realistic given Q2 margin decline, and what EBITDA margin is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on track for both volume growth and EBITDA margin, and reiterated that Q2 is a seasonally soft quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How do trade payables and negative operating cash flow look going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade payables were largely cleared early using IPO money to earn cash discounts; payables are expected to remain in single digits, so operating cash flow should normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What are the penalty clauses for supply shortfalls?
qa_highlights.answer: Most agreements are supply-subject-to-availability with no penalty; some have quarterly minimum guarantees (for example 60% of contracted capacity), and no penalty has been paid historically.

risks_watch: Q3 and Q4 delivery of the guided EBITDA per ton ramp depends on waste-to-steam plant commissioning timelines (Jhagadia, Nandesari, Vapi and a further plant next calendar year).
Volume growth needs H2 FY27 to grow about 35% over H1; any further supplier shutdown or monsoon disruption would slow this.
Coal price pass-through lag (about 15 days) and an enlarged gap between steam revenue growth and volume growth can distort margins.
Return ratios are diluted after the IPO: ROCE of 12.97% and ROE of 4.53% (not annualised).
Himachal Pradesh project: offtake is not committed by the government and pricing is still under negotiation.
Operating cash flow was negative in H1 and trade payables were largely cleared; management expects payables to stay in single digits.

544917|2026-06.headline: Karamtara Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72% YoY to INR1,581 crore, EBITDA INR174 crore (~11% margin), PAT INR87 crore; FY27 growth target 60-65%.
544917|2026-06.overview: Karamtara's first call as a listed company reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR1,581 crore (+72% YoY), EBITDA of INR174 crore (+45% YoY, ~11% margin) and PAT of INR87 crore (+45% YoY). Management said the quarter was hit by elevated freight and tariff-related costs, which it expects to ease, and reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 60-65%. Transmission was flagged as the next major growth driver, with new Bhachau capacity ramping and a Saudi Arabia plant targeted for trials around December. Management gave no FY28 numbers and no explicit margin guidance.

segments.name: Renewables (solar, wind, transmission)
segments.commentary: Renewable products were 82% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management said transmission (about 30% of revenue per an analyst's reading) is the next major growth driver.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Solar revenue grew from about INR20 crore in FY21 to an expected INR5,000-5,500 crore this year, per management. Portfolio includes module mounting structures, tracker piles, torque tubes, couplers, purlins and stamp parts.

segments.name: Transmission
segments.commentary: New Bhachau facility began manufacturing recently; management expects peak capacity within 6-9 months. Lattice towers up to 1,200 kV.

segments.name: PEB (data centre)
segments.commentary: New PEB facility at Bhachau expected to start by the beginning of next financial year, with revenue in FY28 and a larger share after that.

segments.name: Fasteners
segments.commentary: Bolts, nuts, studs and washers for solar, wind, transmission, bridges and railways. Facility moved to Nagpur after a rolling mill there was shut down.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of 60-65% YoY; management said it hopes to beat this internally.
Revenue seasonality: 40-42% in H1 and 58-60% in H2, per management's historical pattern.
EBITDA margin expected to improve as utilisation rises and fixed costs are absorbed; no numerical margin guidance given. Management cited freight normalisation as a further lever.

Saudi Arabia plant: trials around December, galvanizing plant online by February or March, commercial output by end-CY/early next year; 12-18 months to reach strong utilisation; revenue begins next year.
No FY28 revenue guidance; management said strong growth is expected from Saudi, PEB and transmission capex.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity of 889,200 MTPA as of quarter end, excluding captive rolling and galvanizing capacity.
13 manufacturing facilities: 8 in Maharashtra (7 Boisar, 1 Nagpur), 4 in Gujarat (Bhachau), 1 in Italy.
New Bhachau rolling mill for transmission towers and solar tracker piles now ramping; management expects peak capacity in 6-9 months.
Under construction: PEB facility at Bhachau (data centres), solar stamped parts facility at Boisar, multiproduct plant in Saudi Arabia (transmission and solar).
Capex of about INR900 crore in FY26 and continued investment in FY27; management said capex is funded partly by IPO proceeds, with some term loan debt.
demand_pricing: Management said demand continues to outpace supply in the renewables market; large installed capacity allows selective order acceptance.

Contracts: Indian solar contracts run 4-5 months with steel and zinc covered by mill credit (~90 days). Export contracts run 8-9 months with imported raw material. Management says commodity risk is passed through to customers via pass-through or price-variation clauses.

US: steel and aluminium products face a 50% Section 232 tariff, which management says was fully passed through to buyers. US domestic supply of these products is limited; management said local US prices are 30-40% above Indian landed prices, with 6-8 month lead times.
Freight and shipping costs are at elevated levels globally because of fuel prices, which weighed on Q1 margins.
No major real competition from Indian companies in US exports, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy on business mix and transmission share, given strong bidding and pricing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transmission will be a very large growth driver, citing the new Bhachau facility, hybrid wind towers that can be switched to transmission, and the Saudi plant. It plans to build the transmission portfolio as it did solar.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 trend and FY27 guidance on revenue and EBITDA margin.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 has been good and reiterated 60-65% growth for FY27 with H1 at 40-42% of revenue. It said margins will rise with utilisation but gave no numerical guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Contract structure: cost-plus, fixed or mixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic solar contracts are 4-5 months and export contracts 8-9 months, with raw material pass-through. Long-term domestic transmission and some export contracts have price-variation clauses; some large overseas FOB contracts pass shipping through.

qa_highlights.question: Would tariffs erode US export competitiveness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 50% steel tariff under Section 232 is fixed and any further tariffs do not stack. Tariff costs were passed through to buyers, and US buyers face 30-40% higher local prices.

qa_highlights.question: Margin lever: product mix, Saudi or operating leverage? Utilisation path to 75%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will improve as assets are utilised and fixed costs are absorbed, with local-content Saudi output expected to earn better margins. Bhuj and Saudi ramps will take 6-18 months, and the company expects growth to come from all segments.

qa_highlights.question: PEB differentiation and expected margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entry is aimed at data-centre demand, with qualification in the Nordics and existing customer pull. It declined to commit to a margin range but expects margins similar to its other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Tariff-adjusted revenue comparison.
qa_highlights.answer: Tariff pass-through was about INR250 crore in Q1 FY27 versus about INR113 crore in Q1 FY26 and about INR196 crore in the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Volume and other expenses.
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was about 135,000 tonnes. Other expenses of about INR500 crore include tariff and freight costs, which management said are passed on to customers.

544921|2026-06.headline: Arcil Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 107% to INR143 crores on INR1,066 crores recoveries (up 151%), with acquisitions seasonally light at INR353 crores.
544921|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a recovery-led quarter: total recoveries rose 151% to INR1,066 crores and standalone PAT more than doubled to INR143 crores, driven by a large corporate resolution. Acquisitions were INR353 crores (Arcil share INR143 crores), about INR150 crores lower than Q1 FY26, consistent with the seasonal pattern where most acquisitions occur in Q4. AUM was INR19,574 crores (up 16% YoY) and borrowings fell sequentially to INR1,100 crores, with management expecting to draw down more in the coming quarters. Consolidated PAT was INR59 crores versus standalone INR143 crores, and management urged investors to assess the company on a standalone and full-year basis.

Management attributed improved industry recovery rates (cited as moving from about 35% to about 85%) to a stronger economy and real estate recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Why has industry recovery rate risen from about 35% to about 85%, and will it improve further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an improving economy lets ARCs buy cheaply in stress and resolve at higher rates later; real estate assets stressed four to five years ago are now repaying and redeeming SRs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings fall sequentially, and will they be drawn again?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowings are seasonal: lines are drawn mainly at year-end for acquisitions. With a strong pipeline for Q2 and Q3, management expects to draw down more and marginally increase leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Is there AUM guidance for FY27, and why is the retail mix rising?
qa_highlights.answer: No AUM target was given; AUM is expected to rise with acquisitions balanced by equal resolutions, roughly 20-25% of opening AUM resolved each year. Mix reflects asset availability, with no target balance.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the INR120 crore write-back of earlier written-off assets, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Write-backs are event-based recoveries from legal cases. Management cited about INR288 crores in FY24, INR100 crores in FY25 and INR66 crores in FY26, said Q1 should not be a full-year trend, and said maximum write-offs over the next three years total under INR100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is fee income, given fee income is about 2.4% of AUM annualised versus 1.4% a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management fee nearly doubled YoY and is about 45-50% of total fees. Fee income also depends on collections and resolution, not AUM alone. Management said the momentum should be maintained, and fees are earned only on recoveries, with the legacy book carrying no fee.

qa_highlights.question: What are the IRR and vintage profile of the book, and how is the 15% minimum SR investment used?
qa_highlights.answer: General IRR targeted in the high-20s to 20-22% range. Over-8-year vintage AUM is 34%, fully written off on a regulatory basis. Mandatory SR investment is 15%, as low as 2.5% in co-investor deals; own share is 22% of AUM, and Q1 FY27 investment is running at about 40% of acquisitions versus 33% in FY26.

Management attributed the Q2 margin rebound to a 21% rise in average realisation (about 17% price hike, 3.5% mix) plus operating efficiency, after a disrupted Q1 when production stopped in April due to fuel unavailability. Exports fell sharply on container and freight shortages, while domestic GVT volumes grew. Management guided to around 15% value and 10% volume growth for FY27 if exports revive, and said no major capex is planned.

544949|2026-09.headline: Swastika Infra H1 FY27 revenue INR207 crores (+5% YoY), Q2 revenue +42% to INR188 crores; unexecuted order book about INR1,420 crores.

Q2 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR188 crores, EBITDA 62% to INR27 crores and PAT 75% to INR16 crores, while H1 revenue grew only 5% after a weak Q1 that management attributed to component price volatility and supply uncertainty. Management said it went slow in Q1 as a prudent measure and has since geared up. Unexecuted order book is about INR1,420 crores (2.8x FY26 revenue), including a roughly INR600 crore Maharashtra order won in late Q2 with a two-year execution period. Management guided FY27 full-year growth in line with FY26, with H2 seasonally heavier.

segments.name: Transmission
segments.commentary: About 6% of the unexecuted order book; a segment entered in roughly the last one and a half years. Management said transmission has longer site-readiness lags (RoW, component availability) than distribution.

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year growth expected to be in line with FY26, per management qualitative guidance; H2 seasonally heavier.

Year-end FY27 order book targeted at about INR1,500-2,000 crores, dependent on wins in two to three new states, with bids of about INR1,000-1,500 crores planned and a historical success rate of about 30%.

Bill-to-order-book conversion historically about 70-80%+ (per management).

qa_highlights.question: How much order inflow was added in Q2 and what is the guidance for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR900-950 crores of new orders were added over the last six months, including a roughly INR600 crore Maharashtra order at end-Q2 (part of the INR1,420 crore book, two-year execution). Full-year growth expected in line with FY26, with execution visible mainly in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA margin increase and is 14% the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin was a function of revenue mix, with more commissioning and erection work and final milestone billings. Management expects margins to normalise to around 14% on a full-year basis, without exact quantitative guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 decline and what is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was weak due to peak component price volatility and supply uncertainty, so the company deliberately slowed work. Management said annual working capital needs should be roughly equal to H1 requirement, as working capital eases in H2 with government budget clearances.

qa_highlights.question: How will finance costs be controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Near term, IPO proceeds should reduce debt over the next two to four quarters. Longer term, the company is rated BBB+ and aims for an A- upgrade, and a shift from bank guarantees to surety bonds is expected to lower funding costs and working capital needs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order-book breakup and do margins differ by vertical?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution about 85%, renewable about 8%, transmission about 6%. Orders are typically bundled across substations, cabling, instrumentation and RMUs, so margins were not split by vertical.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is executable in the next 6-12 months and are there delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the historical bill-to-order ratio of 70-80%+ as the guide. No delays or liquidated damages historically; distribution has shorter site-readiness lags than transmission.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin is at risk from cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply inputs are protected by contract price variation clauses; labour volatility is limited. It pointed to a track record of maintained margin discipline over four to five years.

qa_highlights.question: Are RDSS and other schemes driving the pipeline, and how is the company positioned for digital and DER work?
qa_highlights.answer: RDSS is currently active only in Rajasthan and Gujarat; the Maharashtra order is ADB-funded and Himachal and West Bengal are World Bank-funded. RDSS phase 2 is announced, with tenders expected soon. The company is not currently pursuing SCADA or AMI work, but has quoted a BESS tender.

544959|2026-06.headline: Runwal Enterprises Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 3,400 million (from Rs 4,462 million) on occupation-certificate-based recognition, while pre-sales rose ~5% to Rs 4,835 million.
544959|2026-06.overview: This was the maiden earnings call after the company's listing, with the IPO proceeds received in the first week of October 2026. Pre-sales rose about 5% YoY to Rs 4,835 million and collections rose to Rs 5,754 million from Rs 4,993 million. Revenue from operations declined to about Rs 3,400 million, which management attributed to revenue being recognised only on occupation certificate and possession. Management said debt has been cut to about Rs 1,900 million external debt post-IPO and debt-to-equity has fallen from about 3 to about 1.5, with fuller benefits visible from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company issue stated guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna Kanodia said no specific guidance yet, but a general direction on growth (20-25% pre-sales) will be given while maintaining balance-sheet and margin health.

qa_highlights.question: Debt repayment plan and current debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said debt-to-equity fell from 3.1x to 1.5x and debt is now about Rs 1,900 crore external. Future borrowing will be limited and self-liquidating. Shashi Bhushan added that land monetisation to data operators is being considered, with JLL mandated and 10-12 interested parties.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the land for the data-centre monetisation and how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Shashi Bhushan said the land is in Dombivli (Gardens and My City, part of a 250-acre parcel); about 18 acres is being considered for sale. No transaction has been concluded.

qa_highlights.question: Lease income profile from BKC and Nexus mall?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said both projects should complete in about 2.5 years, with mall rentals possibly above Rs 100 crore in year one after stabilisation. BKC tenant is still being sought; a rental number is hard to give at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Launch pipeline and approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: Shashi Bhushan said two or three projects await approval, including a Bandra redevelopment and a Marine Drive project, likely launched this year or early next year. Management declined to give launch guidance because approvals are third-party dependent.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the IPO size cut from Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said SEBI offered a one-time option to halve offer size for entities already approved, given weak markets; the offer was all primary (about 10-11% dilution), and bankers advised taking it.

545004|2026-09.headline: Jio Platforms Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.4% YoY to ₹40,475 Cr, EBITDA up 16.6% to ₹21,879 Cr at a 54.1% margin.
545004|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first quarter reported after listing; management reported 542.4 million customers, 36 million YoY net adds and 9.1 million adds in the quarter, with 5G base at 300 million. Management framed growth around four pillars (grow, deepen, convert, build) and pushed a 'digital gateway' model, while explicitly not using tariff hikes as the main ARPU lever. Net leverage was 0.11x at 30 September; the call also covered the IPO (about ₹30,188 Cr of issue proceeds, 24.5x oversubscribed) and international partnership plans.

570004|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 4% to INR1,800 crore and EBITDA about 7%, but a March raw-material shock cost an estimated INR200-250 crore of sales.

UK food revenue rose from GBP 60 million to GBP 68 million, with cost headwinds. Beverage bottling lines (juice and CSD) started in Q4; about INR27-28 crore revenue was booked by end-March.

Farmers postponed purchases in March and April due to price uncertainty and lower prices for farm produce as exports fell.

rows.why: Guidance was held (standalone margin about 14%, consolidated 12-13%) after a weak Q1 with revenue down about 2.5% and adjusted PAT about Rs 3 crore, so an upgrade looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 adjusted PAT was about Rs 3 crore versus Rs 30 crore a year ago, the H2 margin catch-up is unproven, and monsoon and polymer-price headwinds remain, so a guidance cut is possible if H2 falls short.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Biochar plant recently started with impact expected from next fiscal, and Coffee Board orders have started revenue, but no new branded product launch was discussed with numbers.

rows.label: NCD repayment of Rs 680-690 crore
rows.why: Management says internal cash flow is the primary source, with legacy receivable collection, land monetisation and refinancing as options, but Rs 164 crore of EBITDA converted at 78% against about Rs 230 crore due in September.

rows.label: Legacy government receivable collection of Rs 422 crore target
rows.when: FY27 (at least Rs 380 crore over the remaining nine months)
rows.why: Only Rs 60 crore collected in Q1, and about Rs 1,100 crore of receivables is above 180 days, so the collection pace is the key cash lever.

rows.label: Food business IPO
rows.why: Total issue was expected at about Rs 1,000 crore, but the timing depends on market valuations that fell over the past year and has no confirmed date.

tone.note: Management was confident on NCD repayment and the H2 recovery and held FY27 margin guidance, but was defensive on the Q1 weakness and vague on the food IPO timing, Tamil Nadu land sale and refinancing; analysts pressed on receivables over 180 days and working capital.

590003|2026-03.headline: KVB posted record FY26 net profit of INR2,500 crores (+29%) and Q4 NIM of 4.25%, but guides FY27 NIM down to 3.75-3.8% and ROA to 1.7-1.8%.
590003|2026-03.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported record quarterly net profit of INR725 crores and full-year profit of INR2,500 crores (+29%), with full-year NIM of 3.97% above guidance. Total business grew 15% to INR2,14,420 crores, with advances up 17% to INR98,754 crores and deposits up 13% to INR1,15,666 crores, though advances growth moderated in Q4 by conscious choice. Management flagged a shift toward preserving relationships over margins: FY27 credit growth is guided at 1-2% above industry, NIM at 3.75-3.8%, and ROA at 1.7-1.8%. Asset quality stayed stable with GNPA at 0.75% and a one-time INR163 crore prudential provision taken against geopolitically exposed sectors.

financial_highlights.change: Highest quarterly profit in bank history
Includes INR163 crore one-time prudential provision

financial_highlights.value: INR187 crores (Q4); INR744 crores (FY26, 0.75% of loans)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 includes ~INR200 crore Q2 chunky slippages
Cost of deposits down 13 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.value: INR679 crores (FY26) excluding INR139 crore interest recovery

segments.name: Retail advances
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 25% YoY and 3% QoQ, driven by mortgages (+56% YoY) and jewel loans (+61% YoY). Housing loans grew only 2%, and BNPL book stands at INR798 crores after a partner management change.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri book grew 19% YoY (5% QoQ) per the call, with agri jewel loans at 91% of agri and LTV of 55.59%; management also cites 5% growth for the year, which is inconsistent with the 19% figure.

segments.name: Commercial and corporate
segments.commentary: Commercial book grew 11.56% YoY but was flat in Q4; corporate grew 12% YoY, or 20% including credit substitutes (incremental INR969 crores). Growth focused on CRE, capital markets and EPC contractors.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: CASA grew 12%, adding INR3,290 crores vs INR677 crores last year; savings deposits added INR2,505 crores. Bulk deposits grew 9% YoY vs 44% prior year, and CDs of INR1,773 crores were reduced in March.

guidance_outlook: FY27 credit growth guided at 1-2% above industry growth, versus 18% achieved in FY26 (RAM and corporate mix 18-20%, with ~5% flex).
FY27 NIM guided at 3.75-3.8% (management also cited 3.7-3.8% on the call), with exit-Q4 NIM above 4%; drop expected from retail term deposit repricing from April 2026 and lower advance yields.
FY27 ROA guided at 1.7-1.8%; credit cost guided at below 1%.
GNPA below 1.5%, net NPA below 1%, slippages below 1% of the asset book, cost-to-income below 50%, LCR maintained at 115-120%.

Branch expansion of 50 branches in FY27 (38 regular, 7 lite, 5 to be shortlisted), front-loaded into H1. Investment yield enhancement of 15-20 bps via HTM rebalancing; duration to be kept around 4-4.5 years over the medium term.

Management sees no need to raise capital in FY27; profit ploughback to fund growth. Dividend declared at 130%, subject to shareholder approval, with the payout on a larger base after the 1:5 bonus issued last year.
capex_capacity: Plan to open 50 branches in FY27: 38 regular, 7 lite, and 5 yet to be shortlisted; front-loading into H1 to capture benefit in Q2.
Management says capital is not a constraint: CRAR at 18.76% with Tier 1 dominant and RWA-to-total-assets at 55-58%, with room to take it up to around 65% over time.
Loan-against-mutual-fund IT integration is at final stage, expected launch in H1 FY27; premium credit cards planned in FY27.
Digital: 98% of transactions digital; DLite app rated 4.8 on Google Play and 4.6 on Apple App Store, with 2.5 million monthly active users.
demand_pricing: Retail term deposit rates raised in April 2026; new products at 7.2%, with blended incremental cost seen at 7.2-7.5% as senior citizen deposits are 27-30% of total deposits.

Competition on yields has intensified from private and public sector banks; management said concession pricing has moved ahead and it may have to cut rates to existing and new borrowers to retain accounts.
Corporate lending: management chose to lean into BBB-rated accounts with gating conditions, with the stated aim of lifting RWA density, while acknowledging fierce competition for AAA/AA names.
Gold loans: jewel loans are 30% of the book against an internal cap of 35%; agri gold yields are about 10.75-11%, and management plans to cut pricing toward 9.5-9% to limit growth.
Working capital utilisation fell 2-3% across sectors in Q4, as customers ran down lines amid geopolitical uncertainty; textile is flagged as the most exposed sector.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 NIM guidance versus the FY26 beat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 3.75-3.8% for FY27, citing sticky deposit costs, leakage of existing customers to competitors, and the need to concede yields to retain top line, accepting some NIM compromise.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the competitive pressure on yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said concession pricing has moved and the bank has held rates, but it now must cut to retain good accounts. Retaining accounts is a priority over margins; Q4 yield benefit of 16 bps came from repricing of 25-30% of the book.

qa_highlights.question: What sectors received the INR163 crore prudential provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Textiles, ceramics, fertilisers, chemicals, granite and quartz, plus other sectors with direct or indirect geopolitical exposure; provisioning was set on a portfolio basis after sector reviews.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ECL transition and steady-state credit cost be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still reviewing the final RBI ECL guidelines and will share clarity later; FY27 credit cost is guided below 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 credit growth guided lower than FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank chose a prudent, moderated approach in a benign-but-volatile environment to avoid credit cost offsetting yield gains, with capital not the binding constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan LTV and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold loans are capped at 75% LTV for retail and 80-85% for agri, with margin of 20-40%; loans above 75% LTV are under 1-1.5% of the portfolio.

risks_watch: NIM trajectory: FY27 guided at 3.75-3.8% vs 3.97% in FY26, with the retail deposit repricing impact to be seen in Q1 FY27.
Yield pressure from competition and existing-customer leakage in corporate, MSME and LAP segments.
Geopolitical exposure: INR163 crore prudential buffer on textiles, ceramics, chemicals and others; West Asia conflict impact on input costs and working capital demand.
Gold price risk: jewel loans at 30% of book; management says a 40% gold price fall would not breach LTV buffers.
ECL transition impact on steady-state credit cost is not yet quantified.
Wage revision provision from November 2026 (IBA committee not yet formed) is not yet provided.
Deposit franchise: term deposit renewals of 70-75% in retail; the flow of new deposits may be insufficient, which may push up cost of funds.

Answers on capital, ECL and the wage provision were non-committal, with several deferred to later updates.

590003|2026-06.headline: KVB Q1 FY27 net profit rose 45% YoY to INR756 crore, but NIM of 4.26% and sequentially lower write-off recoveries (INR103 crore vs INR216 crore) weigh on the outlook.
590003|2026-06.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported Q1 FY27 net profit of INR756 crore, up 4% QoQ and 45% YoY, with NIM of 4.26% and ROA of 2.11%. Total business grew 16% YoY to INR2,27,267 crore, with advances and deposits each up 6% QoQ. Sequentially, operating profit fell 12% to INR1,096 crore and non-interest income fell 28% to INR442 crore, mainly on lower write-off recoveries and one-offs. Management kept the full-year NIM guidance of 3.7% to 3.8% but said NIM should be above 4% next quarter, and it will review full-year guidance at end-September.

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in INR; growth 32% YoY, 5% QoQ

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri portfolio grew 5% QoQ; agri jewel loans are 92% of agri book. Gold LTV is 63.7% for agri and 56.83% for non-agri.

segments.commentary: Commercial segment grew 6% QoQ, with business banking disbursements up 45% QoQ. Management said Q4 FY26 flat growth was an aberration and expects ~18% growth for the year.
